chapters.title: Chapter 1051
paragraphs: The moment the Grand Sorceress saw a smile spread across Jin Taekyung’s face, which had been turning deathly pale, she instinctively realized how foolish a mistake she’d made.
Shit.
It was an irreparable blunder.
She had loosened the binding spell without thinking because his Kill me if you can had been so unmistakably sincere.
And Jin Taekyung had immediately seen her true intentions in that split-second mistake.
“What? Can’t do it, you crazy bitch?”
The Grand Sorceress bit her lip. He’d hit the mark.
A hunting dog could only tear out its target’s throat when its master gave permission. She didn’t yet have that authority, and her earlier bluster about the natural order had been exposed.
Of course, even so—
Nothing changes. Nothing at all.
The Grand Sorceress thought to herself, then poured her strength back into the Magic that had briefly faltered.
Crack!
The thick, sturdy vines squeezed Jin Taekyung’s neck even tighter, as if they’d never loosened at all.

The gulf in strength between them, so stark in that moment, could not be bridged. Unlike him, with barely a trace of internal energy left, a tremendous force still lay coiled deep within the Grand Sorceress’s body.
And that wasn’t all.
With Jin Taekyung held hostage, even the Fire King and the Bow Saint couldn’t risk a reckless move.
All she had to do now was make the young brat submit.
The Grand Sorceress was certain of it—until she saw the smile on his face, brighter than ever.
...He’s smiling?
She couldn’t understand what it meant. Or rather, she knew instinctively, but her mind refused to accept it.
There was only one thing Jin Taekyung could still do in his helpless state. And surely there wasn’t a lunatic anywhere in the world who would choose suicide.
But—
Crunch!
There was.
That lunatic was right here, before her eyes.
Splatter! Splash!
In that instant, the Grand Sorceress’s eyes opened wide without her meaning to.
Everything was red.
Through the blood sliding down her white veil, she saw Jin Taekyung trembling all over and coughing up blood.
“Th-This...”
A stunned gasp escaped her lips.
There was no doubt. He’d severed his own heart meridian.
Even a massive old tree, one that wouldn’t easily fall to a lumberjack’s axe, couldn’t withstand a colony of ants boring through its bark and into its core.
For a Murim martial artist, severing the heart meridian meant death. Agonizing, but swift.
Why would he go this far?
Frozen for an instant, the Grand Sorceress stared at Jin Taekyung in utter shock.
She’d told him only half the truth. It was nowhere near enough to make him certain of anything—just enough to give him a vague suspicion.
Yet how many people under heaven would throw away their lives without hesitation because they suspected their mere existence threatened someone?
None. Surely none.
The strongest desire humans had was the desire to live. Even someone who made such a choice would need time to doubt, to steel themselves, before carrying it out.
But Jin Taekyung had done it without the slightest hesitation or fear.
Even smiling brightly as he did.
His eyes were already dimming, yet there was no wavering in them. He was certain he’d chosen the right path.
And as she looked at him, the Grand Sorceress finally understood her gravest mistake.
The Chosen One.

Letting him read her intentions earlier was nothing compared to this. She should have understood what those five characters meant. She should have guessed why her great master had searched so long for the young man before her, why he’d ordered his loyal servants to watch his every move.
Jin Taekyung was that kind of person.
He could curse and still know humanity and justice. He could spit and still pursue the chivalrous path. He might walk along the edge of the road, but he would never stray from the right one.
A chivalrous hero who led the way before everyone—and a lunatic beyond anyone’s imagination.
That was why he was the Chosen One.
Crack!
The Grand Sorceress clenched her teeth.
There was no more time to hesitate, no choice left to make.
Her master had already waited far too long. If Jin Taekyung died here today, he would have to wait again, with no end in sight.
I have to save him. Whatever it takes!
As time seemed to slow, the Grand Sorceress reached out, more desperate and frantic than ever.
Swoooooosh!
Immense power surged around her slender frame.

Driven not by the will to kill, but by the will to keep him alive, the energy surrounding her heart pulsed fiercely. The energy dormant in the air answered it, then burst into light and swallowed everything around them.
Flash! Fwoom!
The swelling radiance swept over the hill.
No—it spread until it covered the entire hill.

Its dazzling brilliance bleached the eyes of the Bow Saint and Jeok Cheongang as they raced toward them, having realized something had happened to Jin Taekyung, who was being held hostage. It forced the eyes shut of the fiend, still writhing like an insect as he clung to life.
Even the Grand Sorceress herself, who had summoned that radiance.
What happened?
Her vision lost in the glare, she bit her lip.
When a pile of rocks collapses, it kicks up dust. But when a great mountain crumbles, it causes an earthquake.
A Supreme Peak master who had severed his own heart meridian had suffered an injury not even a Great Firmament Immortal could heal.
She’d unleashed the greatest healing power she could, but there was nothing she could guarantee. And the radiance that had erupted more fiercely than ever showed no sign of fading.
No—at that moment, it seemed to flash even brighter.
Like a blade shining all the more beneath the sun.
Just as the Grand Sorceress’s eyes widened when she realized something—
Shwaaak!
A chillingly low, razor-sharp whistle tore through the air. A silver-white spearhead, more than worthy of the name White Flame, ripped through space.
From beyond the dazzling light came someone’s quiet voice.
“Got you.”
Thud!
My stomach’s churning.
My head’s spinning, and my vision is blurry.
Maybe that’s why I still can’t tell whether this is a dream or reality.
If it’s neither...
Hell? No, heaven?

Everything around me is so white I can barely open my eyes. Unless some enterprising Yama has installed ridiculously powerful LED bulbs throughout hell to improve conditions for its prisoners, this has to be heaven.
But—
Ding. Ding. Diiiing!
Clear chimes ring in my ears like an echo returning from far away. They tell me enough.
This is reality. I’m alive.
I’ve won again at this insane gambling table, where I put up the money I got for selling my life.

System Status Effect: Terrible Internal Injury has been removed! Status Effect: Severe Bleeding has been removed! Status Effect: Exhaustion has been removed! Status Effect: Ruptured Organs has been removed! Status Effect: Fracture has been removed... . . . A powerful healing force takes root in your body! You’ve earned the somehow-you-managed-it achievement: Go Ahead, Gut Me!
Translucent holographic windows appear one after another in midair.
Along with them, my blurry vision cleared as if it had never been blurred. My breathing steadied, and my senses sharpened, letting me feel and take in everything within ten or so jang.
Light. Air. Wind. Even formless things, like the thick stench of blood.
And the living beings breathing amid it all, with the same vitality as me.
Now it was time to collect my winnings from the other side of the bet.
Come.
I whisper the command inwardly and put my will behind it.
I send it toward a cold blade with no life of its own, though it has extinguished countless lives. Toward my beloved weapon, lying alone on the ground far from my hand.
Shwaaak!
It all happens almost at once, and I murmur,
“Got you.”
At that moment—
Thud!
With the sound of bone and flesh bursting, the thick vines binding my entire body loosen.
Now.
I don’t even need to draw on my internal energy. I pour into my limbs a strength beyond anything the word superhuman can describe, and let it loose.
Crack!
The vines split, then burst apart. They snap into pieces under that monstrous force, and I’m free.
I reach out toward White Flame as it shoots toward me like a streak of light.
Tap.
That cool touch is more familiar than anything.
But the blood spattered across the silver-white spearhead is still warm, and the scream that erupts nearby is agonized.
“Aaaah!”
On a battlefield where I can’t see, what could give me a better bearing than a scream?
Following the sharp cry through the lingering radiance, I take one long step.
Bang!
Compressed air explodes beneath my driving foot. The layers of light before me break apart, and the three jang between us vanish in an instant.
And then...
Shaaak!
At the end of the spear’s downward-slashing arc, there was someone who owed me my stake. I could feel exactly where she was, even without seeing her.
Right then—
Swish. Slice!
Dark red blood sprays with a cold cutting sound.
But there’s already no one in the spot where she screamed a moment ago.
Fast.
No. Fast doesn’t begin to describe it.
Any Murim martial artist who saw that movement would call it Shifting Form and Position, a technique only a Supreme Peak master could use.
But no matter what anyone else in this world thought, I was the one exception.
Blink...!
A Magic spell that made you disappear in an instant, like the literal blink of an eye—a short-range teleport.
In a Grand Mage’s hands, it works even faster than Shifting Form and Position. It’s an incredible way to evade an attack—but that’s all it is.
Three steps from my left. Five jang.
I know Blink’s limits better than anyone under heaven.
Crack.
And I’m a superhuman with the strength and senses to catch up with it, despite its limited range.
Boom!
One step.
I cross that distance in an instant and smile brightly at the Grand Mage, frozen with her eyes wide.
“See you again?”
Shing!

chapters.title: Chapter 1052
paragraphs: “See you again?”
At the sound of his low voice, Jin Taekyung was suddenly right in front of her. The Grand Sorceress felt the blood in her body turn cold.
How?
Calling him fast didn’t begin to explain it. His speed was beyond anything she’d expected.
And as though he’d known exactly where she would be, the silver spearhead came slashing down toward her body.
Whoosh!
The air split. No—it shattered.
Space warped around the Force coiling along the spearhead. Faced with that terrifying sight, the Grand Sorceress felt a fear greater than any she had known and cried out in her mind.
Mighty power of protection!
Vwoom.
In the slowed world, the energy gathered around her heart began to boil.
Layer upon layer of translucent shields rose around her, blocking the spearhead.
Boom! Crash!
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck.
But all the Grand Sorceress’s attention was fixed on the sight before her.
The spearhead smashed through most of the dozens of layered shields before finally stopping—just barely.
I blocked it.
A shiver ran up her spine. Only then did she release the breath she’d been holding.
Before relief could settle in, she saw Jin Taekyung smiling faintly, though the attack he’d staked everything on had failed. Suddenly, she realized what she’d forgotten.
Some very important—and very dangerous—people.
But on a battlefield, realizations always came a moment too late.
Whoosh!
A vast streak of light hurtled across the space between them.
Beyond the dazzling glare filling her vision, she made out two figures. The Grand Sorceress screamed without a sound.
The Bow Saint...!
Boom!
An enormous blast rang out, and the swelling light swallowed the entire hill.
At the last moment, it all happened almost at once.
I’d backed away, anticipating the shock of the tremendous collision.
Far away, the Force arrow had left the bowstring and come hurtling toward us. At last, it struck the shield.
And then—
Fwoom!
The distant flash of light swelled, blocking everyone’s view and swallowing the Grand Sorceress’s figure, which had been hidden behind the crumbling shield.
Rumble...!
The earth shook. Light burst forth in an instant, tearing through the darkness and devouring everything.
A wave of power beyond words.
Hngh...!
I sucked in a breath and curled up as tightly as I could. A gale whipped past me like a blade, slashing through the air.
The moment lasted only an instant, but it felt like an eternity. When it passed, I could finally hear again.
A familiar voice reached my muffled ears.
“Are you all right?”
I let out the breath I’d been holding and raised my head.
Beyond the fading light, I saw a white robe torn to shreds, blood scattered everywhere, and limbs severed from a body.
They were slender and white—the limbs clearly belonged to a woman.
“It’s over. All of it.”
The Grand Mage was dead.
The moment that sank in, all the strength drained from my body.
My mental strength had been at its limit for a long time. Exhaustion washed over me, and my vision blurred.
Grab.
A strong hand caught me as I swayed.
Jeok Cheongang hauled me upright, and a laugh escaped me.
“Sorry, Old Master.”
“For what?”
“Seven and a half minutes. That ran out ages ago.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed with me.
“Still a hundred years too soon. Can’t you tell, seeing that damned bastard run all the way over here?”
He was covered in blood, whatever he said. With a perfectly straight face, he pointed to an old fiend who had survived like a cockroach.
Of course, there was another reason the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had survived the blast.
“You went a long way while I was gone. Recklessly far, too.”
So Gyo—or rather, the Bow Saint—looked at me with her usual calm gaze and spoke.
She must have crossed half the land without a moment’s rest, yet her aura was still as sharp as a blade.

I knew better than anyone why the Bow Saint, despite the crushing fatigue she must have felt, was keeping up this front. I also knew why she had gone out of her way to protect the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
“But the rest will have to wait. There’s still a problem to deal with.”
She was right. The Grand Mage was dead, but the bloody battle below the hill continued.
And that wasn’t the only problem she meant.
“So this is how it’s come to pass.”
Cold killing intent edged her words. At her feet, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord lay breathing hard. He struggled to speak.
“Fine. Anything... I’ll tell you anything.”
Anything, huh?
I turned the word over in my mind as I staggered toward him and raised White Flame.
Shing.
I aimed the spearhead at him instead of answering.
Faced with its icy gleam, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s voice grew louder. He was still trying to sound calm.
“There was a traitor among you!”
The fiend who had radiated such terrifying power was nowhere to be seen.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord sprawled before me now was little more than a beggar, ruined at the end of a lifetime steeped in brutality.
Abandoned by his master. Betrayed by his allies. Now begging for his life by selling information to the very enemy he’d tried to kill.
“Are you afraid?”
“...What?”
“Can things like you feel fear?”
I looked down at his wide, bloodshot eyes and spoke softly.
“There’s no deal.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord was already a discarded dog.
Perhaps his fate had been sealed long ago: to be discarded once he’d outlived his usefulness.
I didn’t know the exact reason, but this was the outcome the Lord of Heaven had intended. No master would lavish care on a hunting dog he planned to cast aside without mercy.
So I had no reason to listen to the dog. Least of all when he wanted to talk about the traitors whose identities had begun to come to light today.
“Black Night King Sima Gong. The Roaring Fury Swordsman Song Il. And the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord said nothing, but his eyes shook violently.
That was enough to turn a near-certainty into certainty.
“You already... knew?”
He barely managed to force the words out.
I nodded at his dazed face.
“To a certain extent.”
“B-But then why?”
“If you’re asking why... I don’t know.”
I raised the spearhead, exhaustion bearing down on me.
And I thought about why I’d made it this far, despite suspecting there were traitors among us. Why I’d fought for my life in this impossible situation and refused to give up.
Maybe it was because...
“I wanted to believe a little longer.”
“You can’t win without believing in them. That’s why I came all this way like a fucking idiot.”
Yeah.
That was what made victory possible.
The difference between Dark Heaven and us.
Between the Lord of Heaven and me.
I’d already seen what came of that slender thread of faith and hope. More precisely, of the faith that began with one person.
Sama Pyo.
Quiet and gloomy, but he’d never once betrayed my trust.
A comrade who had never been the first to step back, no matter how desperate things got. We’d fought back to back and laughed together, covered in each other’s blood.
No. A friend.
If it weren’t for him, I wouldn’t have been able to place even this little faith in them.
Not long ago, Jeok Cheongang had asked what I would do if Sama Pyo and Taishan turned out to have betrayed us.
I hadn’t answered.
Even as I walked down the Great Snow Mountain with Sama Pyo, I’d asked myself the same question. But I couldn’t bring myself to answer it.
I wouldn’t be able to kill them.
All I could do was believe. More desperately than anyone.
And I wasn’t the only one who’d put faith in the traitors.
A Junior Brother in his two Senior Brothers. A son in his father.
In the end, their faith was rewarded.
It moved the traitors’ hearts and finally turned the tide of battle.
I’d seen it myself.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword and the Roaring Fury Swordsman throwing themselves toward the Hell Fire. Sima Gong facing the Blood-Sword Demon Lord in Jeok Cheongang’s place.
Of course, they wouldn’t be forgiven for their crimes.
At least, I had no right to forgive them. Neither did Jeok Cheongang or the Bow Saint.
But I would remember that, when it mattered most, the traitors had upheld at least the smallest measure of honor.
Unlike the discarded hunting dog, who would soon be forgotten by its master.
“That’s why we’re different. You and us.”
My voice was quiet, but clear. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at me, the tiny blood vessels in his eyes burst.
“Jin Taekyung!”
His cry came out as though he were coughing up blood.
Thuk.
The spearhead sank into his chest as smoothly as a blade through tofu, swallowing the rest of his words.
No—the last faint trace of life left in him.
Ding.
A clear chime rang in my ears.
At the same time, an energy as refreshing as mountain-stream water swept through me, once again filling my body with new strength.
Unlike the man who had died with a silver-white spearhead through his chest.
And just as the woman who had died moments before, too horribly to leave her body in one piece, had wanted.
I mustn’t fall here? I have to get stronger than I am now?
Feeling the crushing mental exhaustion weighing on my body, I turned to look toward the last trace of the Grand Mage, left behind where the Force arrow had swept through.
Don’t worry. I’ll make sure of it.
I didn’t know what the Lord of Heaven wanted.
But one thing was clear.
I had to keep going. To keep moving forward, I had to grow stronger.
Strong enough to far exceed the Lord of Heaven’s expectations. Strong enough to make him regret this choice someday.
Whatever gets in my way, I’ll just smash it to pieces.
That was how I’d lived until now, and how I’d live from here on.
With that thought, I turned my unsteady body around.
Or I tried to.
Then I saw a slender arm and leg lying in a pool of blood, each severed from her body. Their cut ends were sharp and clean.
No.
Not until I spotted the traces of Teleport.

Faced with that terrifying sight, the Grand Sorceress felt a fear greater than any she had known and cried out in her mind.
Mighty power of protection!
Vwoom.
In the slowed world, the energy gathered around her heart began to boil.
Layer upon layer of translucent shields rose around her, blocking the spearhead.
Boom!
Crash!
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck.
But all the Grand Sorceress’s attention was fixed on the sight before her.
The spearhead smashed through most of the dozens of layered shields before finally stopping—just barely.
I blocked it.
A shiver ran up her spine.
Only then did she release the breath she’d been holding.
Before relief could settle in, she saw Jin Taekyung smiling faintly, though the attack he’d staked everything on had failed.
Suddenly, she realized what she’d forgotten.
Some very important—and very dangerous—people.
But on a battlefield, realizations always came a moment too late.
Whoosh!
A vast streak of light hurtled across the space between them.
Beyond the dazzling glare filling her vision, she made out two figures.
The Grand Sorceress screamed without a sound.
The Bow Saint...!
Boom!
An enormous blast rang out, and the swelling light swallowed the entire hill.
At the last moment, it all happened almost at once.
I’d backed away, anticipating the shock of the tremendous collision.
Far away, the Force arrow had left the bowstring and come hurtling toward us.
At last, it struck the shield.
And then—
Fwoom!
The distant flash of light swelled, blocking everyone’s view and swallowing the Grand Sorceress’s figure, which had been hidden behind the crumbling shield.
Rumble...!
The earth shook.
Light burst forth in an instant, tearing through the darkness and devouring everything.
A wave of power beyond words.
Hngh...!
I sucked in a breath and curled up as tightly as I could.
A gale whipped past me like a blade, slashing through the air.
The moment lasted only an instant, but it felt like an eternity.
When it passed, I could finally hear again.
A familiar voice reached my muffled ears.
“Are you all right?”
I let out the breath I’d been holding and raised my head.
Beyond the fading light, I saw a white robe torn to shreds, blood scattered everywhere, and limbs severed from a body.
They were slender and white—the limbs clearly belonged to a woman.
“It’s over.
All of it.”
The Grand Mage was dead.
The moment that sank in, all the strength drained from my body.
My mental strength had been at its limit for a long time.
Exhaustion washed over me, and my vision blurred.
Grab.
A strong hand caught me as I swayed.
Jeok Cheongang hauled me upright, and a laugh escaped me.
“Sorry, Old Master.”
“For what?”
“Seven and a half minutes.
That ran out ages ago.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed with me.
“Still a hundred years too soon.
Can’t you tell, seeing that damned bastard run all the way over here?”
He was covered in blood, whatever he said.
With a perfectly straight face, he pointed to an old fiend who had survived like a cockroach.
Of course, there was another reason the Blood-Sword Demon Lord had survived the blast.
“You went a long way while I was gone.
Recklessly far, too.”
So Gyo—or rather, the Bow Saint—looked at me with her usual calm gaze and spoke.
She must have crossed half the land without a moment’s rest, yet her aura was still as sharp as a blade.
I knew better than anyone why the Bow Saint, despite the crushing fatigue she must have felt, was keeping up this front.
I also knew why she had gone out of her way to protect the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
“But the rest will have to wait.
There’s still a problem to deal with.”
She was right.
The Grand Mage was dead, but the bloody battle below the hill continued.
And that wasn’t the only problem she meant.
“So this is how it’s come to pass.”
Cold killing intent edged her words.
At her feet, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord lay breathing hard.
He struggled to speak.
“Fine.
Anything...
I’ll tell you anything.”
Anything, huh?
I turned the word over in my mind as I staggered toward him and raised White Flame.
Shing.
I aimed the spearhead at him instead of answering.
Faced with its icy gleam, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s voice grew louder.
He was still trying to sound calm.
“There was a traitor among you!”
The fiend who had radiated such terrifying power was nowhere to be seen.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord sprawled before me now was little more than a beggar, ruined at the end of a lifetime steeped in brutality.
Abandoned by his master.
Betrayed by his allies.
Now begging for his life by selling information to the very enemy he’d tried to kill.
“Are you afraid?”
“...What?”
“Can things like you feel fear?”
I looked down at his wide, bloodshot eyes and spoke softly.
“There’s no deal.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord was already a discarded dog.
Perhaps his fate had been sealed long ago: to be discarded once he’d outlived his usefulness.
I didn’t know the exact reason, but this was the outcome the Lord of Heaven had intended.
No master would lavish care on a hunting dog he planned to cast aside without mercy.
So I had no reason to listen to the dog.
Least of all when he wanted to talk about the traitors whose identities had begun to come to light today.
“Black Night King Sima Gong.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman Song Il.
And the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom.”
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord said nothing, but his eyes shook violently.
That was enough to turn a near-certainty into certainty.
“You already... knew?”
He barely managed to force the words out.
I nodded at his dazed face.
“To a certain extent.”
“B-But then why?”
“If you’re asking why...
I don’t know.”
I raised the spearhead, exhaustion bearing down on me.
And I thought about why I’d made it this far, despite suspecting there were traitors among us.
Why I’d fought for my life in this impossible situation and refused to give up.
Maybe it was because...
“I wanted to believe a little longer.”
“You can’t win without believing in them.
That’s why I came all this way like a fucking idiot.”
Yeah.
That was what made victory possible.
The difference between Dark Heaven and us.
Between the Lord of Heaven and me.
I’d already seen what came of that slender thread of faith and hope.
More precisely, of the faith that began with one person.
Sama Pyo.
Quiet and gloomy, but he’d never once betrayed my trust.
A comrade who had never been the first to step back, no matter how desperate things got.
We’d fought back to back and laughed together, covered in each other’s blood.
No.
A friend.
If it weren’t for him, I wouldn’t have been able to place even this little faith in them.
Not long ago, Jeok Cheongang had asked what I would do if Sama Pyo and Taishan turned out to have betrayed us.
I hadn’t answered.
Even as I walked down the Great Snow Mountain with Sama Pyo, I’d asked myself the same question.
But I couldn’t bring myself to answer it.
I wouldn’t be able to kill them.
All I could do was believe.
More desperately than anyone.
And I wasn’t the only one who’d put faith in the traitors.
A Junior Brother in his two Senior Brothers.
A son in his father.
In the end, their faith was rewarded.
It moved the traitors’ hearts and finally turned the tide of battle.
I’d seen it myself.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword and the Roaring Fury Swordsman throwing themselves toward the Hell Fire.
Sima Gong facing the Blood-Sword Demon Lord in Jeok Cheongang’s place.
Of course, they wouldn’t be forgiven for their crimes.
At least, I had no right to forgive them.
Neither did Jeok Cheongang or the Bow Saint.
But I would remember that, when it mattered most, the traitors had upheld at least the smallest measure of honor.
Unlike the discarded hunting dog, who would soon be forgotten by its master.
“That’s why we’re different.
You and us.”
My voice was quiet, but clear.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord stared at me, the tiny blood vessels in his eyes burst.
“Jin Taekyung!”
His cry came out as though he were coughing up blood.
Thuk.
The spearhead sank into his chest as smoothly as a blade through tofu, swallowing the rest of his words.
No—the last faint trace of life left in him.
Ding.
A clear chime rang in my ears.
At the same time, an energy as refreshing as mountain-stream water swept through me, once again filling my body with new strength.
Unlike the man who had died with a silver-white spearhead through his chest.
And just as the woman who had died moments before, too horribly to leave her body in one piece, had wanted.
I mustn’t fall here?
I have to get stronger than I am now?
Feeling the crushing mental exhaustion weighing on my body, I turned to look toward the last trace of the Grand Mage, left behind where the Force arrow had swept through.
Don’t worry.
I’ll make sure of it.
I didn’t know what the Lord of Heaven wanted.
But one thing was clear.
I had to keep going.
To keep moving forward, I had to grow stronger.
Strong enough to far exceed the Lord of Heaven’s expectations.
Strong enough to make him regret this choice someday.
Whatever gets in my way, I’ll just smash it to pieces.
That was how I’d lived until now, and how I’d live from here on.
With that thought, I turned my unsteady body around.
Or I tried to.
Then I saw a slender arm and leg lying in a pool of blood, each severed from her body.
Their cut ends were sharp and clean.
No.
Not until I spotted the traces of Teleport.

chapters.title: Chapter 1053
paragraphs: The shock was so great that the world seemed to stop. For an instant, Jin Taekyung forgot to breathe.
At the sight of this guess flashing through his mind—a guess he didn’t want to believe—a corner of his chest throbbed as if he’d been stabbed.
“What happened...?”
“Wait. Just a moment.”
Jin Taekyung had gone still as a statue. Jeok Cheongang seemed to realize something and raised a hand, cutting off the Bow Saint’s question.
Of course he knew every moment counted. A fierce battle was still raging below the hill.
But by now, he and his young Disciple understood each other with a glance. They hardly needed even that. The old Master was certain Taekyung had a reason for stopping, and he was right.
Step. Step.
Though he staggered with exhaustion, Taekyung walked on as if entranced.
The scene ahead drew closer, its details coming into sharp focus.
Shreds of a white robe fluttered in a breeze from somewhere. Nearby lay a small pool of blood.
They were the last traces of someone who had been there. Taekyung reached out with a trembling hand and touched the largest of them.
A woman’s arm and leg, slender and so pale that the veins showed through her skin.
Even now, dark red blood was gushing from their cross sections. They were cut with unbelievable precision, smooth and sharp.
As if the limbs hadn’t been cut off, but separated.
This... definitely wasn’t a wound caused by Force.
At last, faced with the truth, Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.
There was no mistaking it. He belonged to two worlds, after all. He was both a Murim martial artist and a Hunter.
That was why he could recognize the marks on the arm and leg, each separated from her body, better than anyone.
“Teleport...”
The word escaped his lips before he knew it. Jeok Cheongang, now beside him, asked with a rigid face, “Tell me it isn’t what this old man thinks.”
Taekyung didn’t answer.
But Jeok Cheongang already knew what his silence meant.
“That bizarre sorcery again. No—Magic?”
Yes. Magic. That damn Magic.
Overcome by a helplessness he couldn’t put into words, Taekyung nodded. Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flashed.
He was already worn down by injuries, both large and small, and by exhaustion. Yet there wasn’t a trace of resignation in those eyes, where flames seemed to pour forth.
“This isn’t the time. Before it’s too late, we need to—”
“It’s already too late.”
“What?”
Taekyung clenched his teeth.
Teleport.
A spatial travel spell notorious for its difficulty, even among the countless kinds of Magic.
Unlike Blink, which was limited to short distances, Teleport could cover dozens or even hundreds of kilometers at once, depending on the mage’s Grade and how much mana they possessed.
Not hundreds of jang. Hundreds of kilometers.
Then how far could Grand Mages, who had reached the limits of Magic, go?
If... every condition were perfect, maybe they could cross half the continent.
Taekyung didn’t know the exact distance. What mattered was that the Grand Mage—a big catch—had already torn through the net and fled far away.
Exhaustion pressed even more heavily on him as he spoke.
“She’s beyond our range. By now, she must be at least dozens of ri away.”
“What do you mean...!”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened, but he swallowed the rest.
Traveling dozens of ri in the blink of an eye was beyond anything reason could account for. Yet he already knew such things were possible. He had seen them with his own eyes.
The inexplicable phenomena tied to Dark Heaven. The ghostly power called Magic, which defied both words and common sense.
“Goddamn it!”
Boom!
Jeok Cheongang stamped his foot in fury, and cracks spread across the ground like a spiderweb.
Through the crash came the Bow Saint’s low voice.
“Even if you’re right, she’s lost an arm and a leg. Her life must be in danger. Is there no chance she died?”
Taekyung shook his head weakly.
“I don’t know. But I doubt it.”
“Why?”
“There must be mages there, too—or sorcerers, as they call them here.”
“Then...”
“Yes. She returned to her allies. We can’t guess where that is, but the Grand Sorceress would have known exactly.”
Jin Taekyung added, staring at the arm and leg submerged in the pool of blood,
“She must have believed she could survive. Otherwise, she wouldn’t have taken a gamble like this.”

Teleport was a difficult spell for long-distance travel. The coordinates of both the starting point and the destination had to be exact, without the slightest error. It demanded more preparation than any other spell.
Even in the modern world, the high-ranking mages who specialized in Teleport and made their living from it were no exception. If anything, knowing the danger made them more careful.
If even the slightest figure went wrong as the spell took effect, they could die instantly, fused with a rock or a tree.
Or...
Their limbs could be separated.
The thought passed silently through Taekyung’s mind. He looked down at the flesh left behind. It was no longer a sign that someone had died.
It was proof that the Grand Mage had gambled her life—and succeeded.
I made a mistake. I should’ve finished her off myself. Made absolutely sure.
He hadn’t expected her to attempt Teleport in the middle of that frantic struggle, with her starting position changing every moment. Much less for the spell to succeed under such unstable conditions.
But regret always arrived a step too late. Taekyung still had to walk the path before him.
The narrow, treacherous path that now seemed clearer and closer—and yet, for some reason, more distant and beyond reach.
Toward the being waiting at its end.
Lord of Heaven.
The title lingered on the tip of his tongue, never spoken. Taekyung turned it over in his mind, bitter as bear gall.
Who was he?
Why was he staining the world with blood and beckoning to Taekyung from behind that dark red curtain?
And what connection did he have to the other being who had haunted Taekyung’s thoughts for so long?
The Demon King. Asmodeus.
Ruler of the Demon Realm. Lord of demons.
An invader who’d torn through the boundaries between dimensions with his overwhelming power, shattered every convention and civilization, and driven billions of people to terror and death.
Yet in the end, he had fallen at the hands of one human. Now he would be remembered forever as part of history.
That’s right. He’s dead. I know he is.
Then why?
Why couldn’t Taekyung get that accursed being out of his head?
Crack.
He bit his lip until it bled.

Over the years he’d spent moving between the modern world and Murim, he’d seen countless lights and shadows. But the darkness cast by Dark Heaven was deeper than any of them. The Lord of Heaven stood at the center of it all, and Taekyung could scarcely deny his existence any longer.
First came all those strange phenomena that overturned everything he knew. Now, Magic.
What the hell is waiting at the end of this?
Taekyung turned his head toward somewhere far to the west.
The Demon King and the Lord of Heaven.
The Lord of Heaven and the Demon King.
He didn’t know whether they’d originally been one being or two entirely different people. The greatest enemy of his life was somewhere beyond the western horizon.
Beckoning to the Chosen One.
For a reason no one else yet knew.
Even knowing that, Taekyung had to keep walking the path he had chosen. Quietly, desperately, with everything he had.
Splash.
He rose, his foot landing in the pool of blood, and forced himself to take a step.
The battle wasn’t over. Countless enemies were still killing and dying like soulless puppets. He headed toward them to finish it.
“Can you hold on?”
“No.”
His Master was watching him with concern. Taekyung looked ready to collapse, but he gave him a faint smile.
“But I have to. Somehow.”
In the past and in the present, that was what he had always done.
Whoosh!
Taekyung charged toward the enemy without hesitation, shoulder to shoulder with his old Master. Force arrows were already streaking through the air above them.
And the three of them weren’t the only ones racing toward the battlefield to end this vast, horrific fight.
Bwooo!
A horn sounded without warning. Those who turned toward it saw a pale cloud of dust sweeping across the vast range of the Great Snow Mountain toward the battlefield.
At the head of thousands of men and horses, a group waved a torn banner and shouted as if coughing up blood.
“Subdue the Demons! Destroy Heaven!”
Hundreds of voices, charged with pure internal energy, burst through the air. The banner billowed in the wind as it advanced with them.
Neither the blood spattered across its white cloth nor the pieces torn from it could erase what it stood for.
It was their pride.
Long ago, it had also been a line of verse written by an old man called the Poet Sage, praising the Daoists who lived in the remote mountain valleys.
“With one long sword to guard the body, one would seek support from Kongtong.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice scattered on the wind. Then the Bow Saint parted her tightly closed lips.
“If you would defend yourself with a single long sword, turn to Kongtong.”
And at that moment—
Rrrrrumble!
In less than two shichen, this brutal battle had swallowed more than ten thousand lives.
Now the scales that would decide its outcome tipped completely.
No—they broke.
Just as some unknown person, somewhere thousands of ri away, had intended when they prepared the stage for this day.

chapters.title: Chapter 1054
paragraphs: “Awaken.”
Nothing more was needed.
The brief whisper roused her mind as it sank beneath the surface of sleep and took hold of her thoughts. Her eyelids, shut tight and motionless until now, opened.
“Ah.”
A short gasp escaped her.
At last conscious again, the Grand Sorceress looked at the pitch-black darkness pressing in from every side and understood.
The gamble she had taken in her final moments, risking her life, had succeeded.
It was also why she was still alive despite the wound that should have killed her.
“Heaven above and earth below, all demons bow in reverence!”
The Grand Sorceress cried out the eight characters of the sacred words engraved upon her soul, then hurriedly prostrated herself before the deep darkness.
First she dropped to both knees, then placed both arms on the ground. Finally, she struck her forehead against the stone hard enough to make it ring.
Thud. Thud. Thud.
Blood drops fell onto the cold stone floor as pain throbbed through her forehead, but the Grand Sorceress paid them no mind.
She could prostrate herself like this—and had recovered the arm and leg torn away when she was swept into unstable space—only through the grace of one being.
“This foolish and lowly servant presents herself before the great Lord of Heaven.”
At the reverence in the Grand Sorceress’s voice, the darkness surrounding her rippled slowly.
“Speak. Tell me everything you saw and heard.”
The brief command echoed inside her mind.
But the Grand Sorceress knew better than anyone that her master wasn’t asking who had won the battle.
His attention was fixed on one person alone.
“I sought to carry out the Lord of Heaven’s command, even at the cost of my life.”
Not daring to raise her face, the Grand Sorceress continued.
She told him roughly how many of their allies Jin Taekyung had killed, how many Black Ghosts had fallen in the process, and how the battle had unfolded from beginning to end.
“And so, shameful as it is, I had no choice but to flee in haste. Please, kill me.”
When she had finished, the Grand Sorceress quietly bit her lip.
She had done everything she could, but not all of it had gone perfectly according to plan.
Then, as she waited in fear, his voice sounded in her mind again.
“You did not see the Blood-Sword’s life taken?”
“...No. Nor did I foresee that the two Daoists of the Zhongnan Sect and Sima Gong would betray us again. Even if I had ten mouths, I would have no excuse.”
There was the Black Night King Sima Gong, who had joined forces with the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
Then there were the Roaring Fury Swordsman Song Il and the Taeeul Merciless Sword Hwangbo Eom, whom Sima Gong had drawn in.

The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, who had recruited the traitors starting with the Black Night King, had known nothing of it. Under the original plan, they should all have been dead by now—killed by Jin Taekyung before the real battle even began.
“But things went wrong somewhere I never expected, even before that.”
“What was it?”
“Kongtong.”
The Kongtong Sect.
They were to be the first supporting players on the stage the Grand Sorceress had prepared.
The Kongtong Sect survivors who had fled Dunhuang were supposed to join their allies in the rear and give a detailed account of everything they had seen and heard.
Dark Heaven’s overwhelming forces. The strange power called Magic.
And, finally, the crucial seed of suspicion that would expose the traitors. That was what the Grand Sorceress had intended to plant.
“So I let word of the traitors reach their ears. Then I let them go, pretending I couldn’t find them.”
She hadn’t failed to catch them.
She had let them go. Deliberately.

It was an audacious claim to make about the Kongtong Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but the Grand Sorceress remained certain of it. Had she and the mages under her command joined the pursuit intent on killing, the Kongtong Sect would have been wiped out in Dunhuang.
But she had made no effort to capture and kill them.
Unlike the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, her goal wasn’t victory.
The separate order she had received from the Lord of Heaven concerned only Jin Taekyung’s survival and growth.
That was why some of the Kongtong Sect had been allowed to survive.

When she heard that their survivors, including the Sect Leader, had shaken off the relentless pursuit and escaped the encirclement, the Grand Sorceress had smothered a laugh to keep the Blood-Sword Demon Lord from noticing. She had already been thinking of what would come next.
The survivors would return and reveal the truth. Jin Taekyung would execute the handful of traitors, become a new rallying point for Dark Heaven’s enemies, and lead them to a sweeping victory.
A safe and perfect plan.
But...
“Some of the survivors who knew the truth, including the Kongtong Sect’s Sect Leader, vanished without a trace.”
The darkness rippled sharply.
“Vanished without a trace?”
“Yes. Forgive me, but even with the power of the sorcery you granted this servant, I could not find them. At some point, they disappeared to a place I cannot even guess.”
The first unexpected crack had appeared, but even the Grand Sorceress could not follow their trail.
Time passed. The real battle began. More cracks appeared, one after another.
For some reason, the traitors had chosen the foolish path again, even with the battle turning against them.
Jin Taekyung had severed his own heart meridian and gambled his life.
And the arrival of the Fire King and the Bow Saint had put the Grand Sorceress herself in danger.
“Please punish this lowly servant for failing to carry out your heavenly command.”
She had achieved her immediate objective, but only that.
The Grand Sorceress lowered her head further and waited for her master’s fury to shake heaven and earth.
But contrary to her fears, the mind-voice that echoed from deep within her a moment later, as if resonating, was as emotionless as ever.
“Raise your head.”
The Grand Sorceress obeyed as if entranced. Beyond the closely woven veil over her face, the darkness writhed as though alive.
It was deeper and denser than she had ever seen it in the past several decades.
“Can you see it? Can you feel it?”
The Grand Sorceress didn’t answer.
No—she couldn’t.
Her pupils, which had rolled back until their whites showed at the sight of the darkness, were already turning black.
“I can see it. I can feel it. Everything hidden inside you. Clearly.”
Whoosh.
The darkness that had completely consumed her retinas didn’t stop there. It continued to spread.
Faster. Deeper.
It took hold of its loyal servant’s mind as her slender body trembled and her reason slipped away. It swept through her thoughts and shook her spirit before returning to its master.
As if nothing had happened.
Thump.
“Ah—hah. Hah!”
The moment the darkness left her eyes and their focus returned, the Grand Sorceress collapsed like a puppet with its strings cut, gasping for breath.
“L-Lord of Heaven.”
Her voice quivered. Her eyes were full of fear.
She knew instinctively what had happened.
The Lord of Heaven had just looked through every one of her thoughts and memories.
At the same time, an awe so intense it raised goose bumps drove out her fleeting fear and enveloped her whole body.
That power...
Remembering the power that had seeped into her body and seized her soul, the Grand Sorceress shuddered.
She knew it had been only a tiny fragment of his power. That made her wonder and shock all the greater.
Just how far can his power reach?
Even a thousand-year-old tree could never touch the clouds.
But the Lord of Heaven was different.
From the moment she had first met him, he had been the absolute ruler, beyond compare. And day by day, he had grown stronger to a degree that made the very word limit meaningless.
The change astonished even the Grand Sorceress, one of his closest confidants.
And she already had an idea where this unbelievable change had begun.
Jin Taekyung. No—the Chosen One.
She was certain of it.
A little more than two years ago, when bloodshed swept through Shanxi Province and the epithet Hidden Dragon became known throughout the land, her master had begun to change as well.

He started waking more often from deep slumbers that had lasted nearly a year at their shortest and as long as ten years. Each time, the Grand Sorceress could feel that the Lord of Heaven had grown stronger.
Even here, today.
But what could that possibly have to do with—?
It was a natural question.
But the next moment, a thunderous echo shook her mind, turning her thoughts blank.
“It is not your place to question anything.”
“Do not forget what your master wants. Do not forget what you must do.”
The Lord of Heaven’s voice seemed to pierce her soul. The Grand Sorceress realized she had momentarily forgotten something.
That the being before her was an absolute ruler, transcending everything.
To serve and worship him as her master, she could permit herself no questions or doubts.
“Please, please kill this irreverent servant!”
The Grand Sorceress cried out as if she were coughing up blood.
Pressed so close to the cold stone floor she seemed ready to become part of it, she reaffirmed her fanatical loyalty and praised her master.
She went on until her voice, once as clear and calm as a silver bell, grew hoarse and cracked.
Until her master finally issued his command to the lowly servant who had dared, even for an instant, to harbor a question.
“That is enough.”
Rustle.
The darkness rippled gently and wrapped around the Grand Sorceress, as though caressing her.
“Nothing of the sort will ever happen. Your master knows that, unlike the Blood-Sword, that foolish hunting dog, your loyalty is steadfast and pure.”
“Lord of Heaven...!”
“Go to the place that awaits you. Join forces there with another of your master’s loyal servants and complete a new mission. The great plan is now truly close to completion.”
Her master’s trust came through more clearly than ever. Overcome, the Grand Sorceress began to weep.
“I will risk my life to fulfill the mission entrusted to me.”
“I believe you. Just as I always have.”
As his quiet voice echoed in her mind, some of the darkness wrapped around the Grand Sorceress sank deep into her body.
No—it seeped into her as if they had always been one.
Whoosh.
The Grand Sorceress shuddered as an unprecedented energy surged from deep within her.
She could sense what the immense new power her master had given her wanted at that very moment—and where it was leading her.
Qinghai.
At that instant—
Whoom!
A brilliant white flash suddenly swelled and burst outward, engulfing her slender body.
Pop.
It all happened in an instant, and ended in an instant.
The Grand Sorceress vanished without a trace. Alone in that pitch-black space, the absolute being murmured quietly.
“Time is passing.”
As the darkness slowly dispersed, an unidentified green light glimmered faintly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1055
paragraphs: Time kept flowing, just as it always had.

It had flowed while the conversation between master and servant ended somewhere in a darkness whose distance and exact location were unknown. And it flowed now, as a young man stopped in the middle of a snowfield that had lost its pure white to blood.
Slosh.
Cold. Sticky.
The blood pooled around his ankles held the deaths of dozens of people. It was also the future of someone standing in it, waiting for death to draw near.
“So this is where you were.”
Kh—cough.
At the young man’s sudden words, the Black Night King Sima Gong blinked through a labored cough.
A face almost exactly like his own appeared in his bleary eyes. He had thought he would never see it again in this life.
His words trailed off.
His surprise lasted only a moment. He studied the son who had returned, then spoke in the same calm voice as always.
“I thought you’d gone far away. Why have you come back here?”
“It was too far for me. As I am now.”
The young man, Sama Pyo, answered, then abruptly turned his head to look somewhere.
Amid the unending roar of battle, powerful fighters swept through the remaining enemies, scattering destructive flashes of light. At their center stood Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
“Perhaps... it wasn’t time yet.”
Sama Pyo had wanted to reach him, but couldn’t. He had wanted to help, but in the end had no choice but to turn back.
He knew why the few hundred jang between him and Jin Taekyung had felt like tens of thousands of ri: he wasn’t strong enough.
Yet part of him stubbornly denied something else—the real reason he had come back.
“So, of all the roads you could have taken, you chose to return here?”
“I only happened to see you.”
You.
It was a dry way to address his father. Sima Gong merely nodded.
“By chance. Yes, I see.”
“Yes. By chance. All of it.”
Whatever they said, father and son both knew this was no coincidence. It was a choice.
Neither saw any need to say so. In that, too, they resembled each other more than anyone else.
“How is the battle going?”
“Is that really what matters to you? When you might stop breathing at any moment?”
“My death is in the future. The battle is happening now. Nothing matters more than what’s before us.”
His father was at death’s door, yet his answer was as firm as ever. Sama Pyo let out a hollow laugh before he could stop himself.
“It’s practically over. The enemy leaders are all dead or have fled. The rest will be wiped out soon.”
It was the plain truth, no more and no less.
The scales that had once tipped toward Dark Heaven’s victory had long since shattered. The Blood-Sword Demon Lord and the mages were dead, and the Grand Sorceress had vanished like a phantom.
Even the powerful Black Ghosts were gone. With the mysterious reinforcements led by the Kongtong Sect now on the battlefield, the allied forces were fighting like men possessed.
Before long, the battle that had stained this vast snowfield red would be over.
No. It was already over.
All that remained was slaughter carried on in the name of battle.
Only after hearing all this did Sima Gong, whose fading consciousness had kept him from knowing it, give a small nod.
“A great victory.”
“A great victory. Ours.”
“Ours. Yes, I suppose you can think of it that way now. The Kongtong Sect may see things differently, of course.”
“The Kongtong Sect...?”
“Don’t pretend you don’t know. You’ve guessed already, haven’t you? The crushing defeat at Dunhuang was no accident.”
Despite the unforgivable crime of betrayal, Sima Gong confessed with pride and composure to the son who resembled him more than anyone else.

“Yes. It’s just as you suspect. I goaded the Gansu sects that opposed me into banding together with the Kongtong Sect to defend Dunhuang, then passed information to the Blood-Sword Demon Lord. I knew what was happening beyond the desert, but I didn’t tell them. If it weren’t for those mounted bandits who came from Ningxia, things wouldn’t have gone the way they did.”
“Are you surprised? Angry? Whatever you think of this old man, I have no regrets. I made a choice for gain and survival. Nothing more.”
Sima Gong looked his son straight in the eye.
Gain and survival.
Yes. That was all. It always had been.

He had lived his entire life as a member of the unorthodox faction. To build up a force weaker than the Demonic Path or the orthodox faction—even weaker than the dark-path figures—he had always had to take dangerous gambles.
Just as, after careful calculation amid the great upheaval of the Great Faction War, he had chosen the orthodox faction and claimed the rights of the victors.
His son stood looking down at him in silence. Then he spoke.
“Why did you do it?”
“I’ve told you everything.”
“I’m not asking why you betrayed them. I know what kind of man you are.”
“Then what are you asking...?”
“Why did you make that choice? You, who pursued survival and gain so ruthlessly. Why?”
At the look in his son’s eyes, Sima Gong finally understood what he was asking. What answer he wanted.
A brief silence stretched between them, long as an eternity. When Sima Gong spoke, his voice was low and cold.
“You still have a long way to go.”
“What... What does that mean?”
“What’s done is done. The reason doesn’t matter. As my heir, you should be asking what comes next. That’s what it takes to be a Sect Leader.”
“Everything will soon be yours. The household and the sect, vast lands and untold wealth... and, most importantly, the grudges you’ll have to settle. Yet you’re curious about the past?”
Sima Gong let out a mocking laugh at his heir.

“I judged you wrongly. You’ll soon gain half of Gansu, only to lose it all. Wolves and vultures will catch the scent of blood and descend from every direction to tear the Black Dragon Demon Gate apart.”

Thousands had died in Dunhuang alone because of his betrayal. The Kongtong Sect had suffered losses comparable to, perhaps even greater than, those it had suffered in the Great Faction War. The same was true of the many sects that formed the roots of Gansu’s martial world.

Sima Gong knew what would happen if the truth came out. If Dark Heaven, betrayed for the second time, let even a little information slip, the name of the Black Dragon Demon Gate would disappear from the world.

Even the Zhongnan Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, might not escape. The crimes of the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword—whether either man was alive or dead—might force the sect to close its gates.
But...
Even when the sky falls, there’s a way out. There always is.
Just as Sima Gong murmured to himself, Sama Pyo, who had been watching him with an indescribable expression, finally opened his firmly closed lips.
“There’s another way.”
“What?”
“A way to save the Black Dragon Demon Gate. A way past the wolves and vultures gathering on every side.”
For an instant, a strange glint flashed in Sima Gong’s eyes.
“Blood is repaid with blood. That is the law of the martial world. They will never forget what the Black Dragon Demon Gate has done.”
“Half right, half wrong,” Sama Pyo said quietly. “Blood should be repaid with blood. But not everyone in the Black Dragon Demon Gate needs to bleed.”
“Am I wrong?”
A heavy silence fell between them.
Screams and shouts still rang out, yet for a moment it seemed every sound around them had vanished.
At last, Sima Gong spoke, his voice low.
“Yes, you’re right. The body itself is innocent. It only did what the head told it to. Isn’t that so?”
Sama Pyo answered calmly.
“If the head doesn’t satisfy them, I’ll have to be prepared to cut off the limbs one by one.”
“So you mean to cut down this old man and the senior members who followed my orders. Every last one.”
“Too many guests will come bearing grudges. Even if each takes only a sip to wet his throat, they’ll need a great deal of blood.”
“Guests, is it? If you’re receiving guests rather than facing enemies, you’ll have to make the arrangements yourself. You’ll be the host soon.”
“If I cut off the head and arms myself and offer them up, along with reasonable compensation, their grounds for revenge will lose their force.”
“Yes. I suppose they would. Though some may call a son who kills his father with his own hands a monster who has forsaken filial duty...”
“More will call me a hero of turbulent times. A Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness, willing to forsake even filial duty for the world and the greater good.”
At that answer, given without hesitation, Sima Gong stared at his son, his face rigid.
His son had just said he would kill his own father.
Then Sima Gong smiled as though his face had never stiffened.
“Truly excellent.”
Forgetting for a moment even the terrible agony that wracked his whole body, the giant who had ruled the unorthodox faction for decades burst into a hearty laugh.
“Yes. This is what I wanted to see from you. This is why I chose you as my heir.”
At that moment, the Black Night King Sima Gong was genuinely happy. He had chosen well. Everything he had built over a lifetime would pass to a worthy successor.
Eight sons and nine daughters. Sama Pyo was his eighth son and his seventeenth and last child.

The youngest and most talented of them all had been his true heir. Now, at last, he had grown into a proper member of the unorthodox faction: a man who could kill even his own father and pursue gain and survival with a cool head in any circumstance.
This is enough.
At the end of his long, hard-fought life, Sima Gong was ready to accept death with a smile of relief.

At the same time, he parted his bloodied lips to speak to Sama Pyo, who was lifting his treasured weapon, the Black Dragon Saber, out of the pool of blood. He addressed the son who had grown from an immature young man into the master of a sect and the new ruler of the unorthodox faction.
“Go ahead and cut me down, Sect Leader.”
At the instant his unfailingly polite voice rang out—
Shwaa!
A brilliant streak of light flashed past his eyes.

He had wanted to help, but in the end had no choice but to turn back.
He knew why the few hundred jang between him and Jin Taekyung had felt like tens of thousands of ri: he wasn’t strong enough.
Yet part of him stubbornly denied something else—the real reason he had come back.
“So, of all the roads you could have taken, you chose to return here?”
“I only happened to see you.”
You.
It was a dry way to address his father.
Sima Gong merely nodded.
“By chance.
Yes, I see.”
“Yes.
By chance.
All of it.”
Whatever they said, father and son both knew this was no coincidence.
It was a choice.
Neither saw any need to say so.
In that, too, they resembled each other more than anyone else.
“How is the battle going?”
“Is that really what matters to you?
When you might stop breathing at any moment?”
“My death is in the future.
The battle is happening now.
Nothing matters more than what’s before us.”
His father was at death’s door, yet his answer was as firm as ever.
Sama Pyo let out a hollow laugh before he could stop himself.
“It’s practically over.
The enemy leaders are all dead or have fled.
The rest will be wiped out soon.”
It was the plain truth, no more and no less.
The scales that had once tipped toward Dark Heaven’s victory had long since shattered.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord and the mages were dead, and the Grand Sorceress had vanished like a phantom.
Even the powerful Black Ghosts were gone.
With the mysterious reinforcements led by the Kongtong Sect now on the battlefield, the allied forces were fighting like men possessed.
Before long, the battle that had stained this vast snowfield red would be over.
No.
It was already over.
All that remained was slaughter carried on in the name of battle.
Only after hearing all this did Sima Gong, whose fading consciousness had kept him from knowing it, give a small nod.
“A great victory.”
“A great victory.
Ours.”
“Ours.
Yes, I suppose you can think of it that way now.
The Kongtong Sect may see things differently, of course.”
“The Kongtong Sect...?”
“Don’t pretend you don’t know.
You’ve guessed already, haven’t you?
The crushing defeat at Dunhuang was no accident.”
Despite the unforgivable crime of betrayal, Sima Gong confessed with pride and composure to the son who resembled him more than anyone else.
“Yes.
It’s just as you suspect.
I goaded the Gansu sects that opposed me into banding together with the Kongtong Sect to defend Dunhuang, then passed information to the Blood-Sword Demon Lord.
I knew what was happening beyond the desert, but I didn’t tell them.
If it weren’t for those mounted bandits who came from Ningxia, things wouldn’t have gone the way they did.”
“Are you surprised?
Angry?
Whatever you think of this old man, I have no regrets.
I made a choice for gain and survival.
Nothing more.”
Sima Gong looked his son straight in the eye.
Gain and survival.
Yes.
That was all.
It always had been.
He had lived his entire life as a member of the unorthodox faction.
To build up a force weaker than the Demonic Path or the orthodox faction—even weaker than the dark-path figures—he had always had to take dangerous gambles.
Just as, after careful calculation amid the great upheaval of the Great Faction War, he had chosen the orthodox faction and claimed the rights of the victors.
His son stood looking down at him in silence.
Then he spoke.
“Why did you do it?”
“I’ve told you everything.”
“I’m not asking why you betrayed them.
I know what kind of man you are.”
“Then what are you asking...?”
“Why did you make that choice?
You, who pursued survival and gain so ruthlessly.
Why?”
At the look in his son’s eyes, Sima Gong finally understood what he was asking.
What answer he wanted.
A brief silence stretched between them, long as an eternity.
When Sima Gong spoke, his voice was low and cold.
“You still have a long way to go.”
“What...
What does that mean?”
“What’s done is done.
The reason doesn’t matter.
As my heir, you should be asking what comes next.
That’s what it takes to be a Sect Leader.”
“Everything will soon be yours.
The household and the sect, vast lands and untold wealth... and, most importantly, the grudges you’ll have to settle.
Yet you’re curious about the past?”
Sima Gong let out a mocking laugh at his heir.
“I judged you wrongly.
You’ll soon gain half of Gansu, only to lose it all.
Wolves and vultures will catch the scent of blood and descend from every direction to tear the Black Dragon Demon Gate apart.”
Thousands had died in Dunhuang alone because of his betrayal.
The Kongtong Sect had suffered losses comparable to, perhaps even greater than, those it had suffered in the Great Faction War.
The same was true of the many sects that formed the roots of Gansu’s martial world.
Sima Gong knew what would happen if the truth came out.
If Dark Heaven, betrayed for the second time, let even a little information slip, the name of the Black Dragon Demon Gate would disappear from the world.
Even the Zhongnan Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, might not escape.
The crimes of the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword—whether either man was alive or dead—might force the sect to close its gates.
But...
Even when the sky falls, there’s a way out.
There always is.
Just as Sima Gong murmured to himself, Sama Pyo, who had been watching him with an indescribable expression, finally opened his firmly closed lips.
“There’s another way.”
“What?”
“A way to save the Black Dragon Demon Gate.
A way past the wolves and vultures gathering on every side.”
For an instant, a strange glint flashed in Sima Gong’s eyes.
“Blood is repaid with blood.
That is the law of the martial world.
They will never forget what the Black Dragon Demon Gate has done.”
“Half right, half wrong,” Sama Pyo said quietly.
“Blood should be repaid with blood.
But not everyone in the Black Dragon Demon Gate needs to bleed.”
“Am I wrong?”
A heavy silence fell between them.
Screams and shouts still rang out, yet for a moment it seemed every sound around them had vanished.
At last, Sima Gong spoke, his voice low.
“Yes, you’re right.
The body itself is innocent.
It only did what the head told it to.
Isn’t that so?”
Sama Pyo answered calmly.
“If the head doesn’t satisfy them, I’ll have to be prepared to cut off the limbs one by one.”
“So you mean to cut down this old man and the senior members who followed my orders.
Every last one.”
“Too many guests will come bearing grudges.
Even if each takes only a sip to wet his throat, they’ll need a great deal of blood.”
“Guests, is it?
If you’re receiving guests rather than facing enemies, you’ll have to make the arrangements yourself.
You’ll be the host soon.”
“If I cut off the head and arms myself and offer them up, along with reasonable compensation, their grounds for revenge will lose their force.”
“Yes.
I suppose they would.
Though some may call a son who kills his father with his own hands a monster who has forsaken filial duty...”
“More will call me a hero of turbulent times.
A Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness, willing to forsake even filial duty for the world and the greater good.”
At that answer, given without hesitation, Sima Gong stared at his son, his face rigid.
His son had just said he would kill his own father.
Then Sima Gong smiled as though his face had never stiffened.
“Truly excellent.”
Forgetting for a moment even the terrible agony that wracked his whole body, the giant who had ruled the unorthodox faction for decades burst into a hearty laugh.
“Yes.
This is what I wanted to see from you.
This is why I chose you as my heir.”
At that moment, the Black Night King Sima Gong was genuinely happy.
He had chosen well.
Everything he had built over a lifetime would pass to a worthy successor.
Eight sons and nine daughters.
Sama Pyo was his eighth son and his seventeenth and last child.
The youngest and most talented of them all had been his true heir.
Now, at last, he had grown into a proper member of the unorthodox faction: a man who could kill even his own father and pursue gain and survival with a cool head in any circumstance.
This is enough.
At the end of his long, hard-fought life, Sima Gong was ready to accept death with a smile of relief.
At the same time, he parted his bloodied lips to speak to Sama Pyo, who was lifting his treasured weapon, the Black Dragon Saber, out of the pool of blood.
He addressed the son who had grown from an immature young man into the master of a sect and the new ruler of the unorthodox faction.
“Go ahead and cut me down, Sect Leader.”
At the instant his unfailingly polite voice rang out—
Shwaa!
A brilliant streak of light flashed past his eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1056
paragraphs: Shwaa!
The flash that tore through the wind was razor-sharp and perfectly aimed.
The Black Dragon Saber.

It was the first and last treasured blade his father had given him. He had been only a boy in his teens then, though he’d distinguished himself so early that his youth hardly mattered. Now the blade followed its master’s hand and cut cleanly through the target before him.
Shhk!
Blood sprayed with a cold slicing sound. The pair of eyes that had watched it all sank deeply.
“What have you done?”
The question held a great deal, but the answer was simple.
“Because this isn’t the path I want.”
Sama Pyo let go of the hilt, cold beneath his hand.
The keen blade, permitted only to the heir of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, had grazed the bridge of Sima Gong’s nose and cut through the pool of blood.
As if mocking the father who had rejoiced to see his son become a true man of the unorthodox faction—and had willingly accepted death.
“This is my choice. The path I, Sama Pyo, have chosen as the man who will succeed you as Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate.”
Sama Pyo calmly met Sima Gong’s gaze as his father shouted, his voice thick with blood.
“Because it isn’t right.”
“What?”
“Because it isn’t what comes first—or what’s best.”
For Sama Pyo, this wasn’t a question of what came first.
It was a question of what was right—of what was better.
“I’d forgotten for my whole life. No—I’d grown so used to it that I kept pretending not to know. But not anymore.”
His life in Gansu had been one long struggle.
Like the siblings born before him, the youngest of the Sama family had fought desperately to avoid being cast aside.
They were family, bound by blood, and rivals competing for the one position of heir. They were little more than soldiers obeying the man who had given them that blood.
Soldiers who sometimes had to face even death.
“Father, Second Brother...!”
“I’ve already heard from the messenger. We’ll hold the funeral after we’ve wiped them all out. Understand?”
Sima Gong had been a cold conqueror. Unifying the unorthodox faction demanded blood and sacrifice.

It was an open secret that more than five of Sama Pyo’s brothers and sisters had died as the Black Dragon Demon Gate brought every unorthodox faction in the land under its banner and rose to stand alongside the Kongtong Sect.
But no one knew that the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s youngest Young Master, chosen as heir while still in his teens, wasn’t as cold as he seemed.
“Why are you crying so bitterly?”
“Father helped Black Dragon Demon Gate. But he died. Taishan sad.”
“Need to find body. Taishan needs to bury father. But, but those people said they don’t know. Taishan sad.”
“...You said your name was Taishan. Come with me.”
Sama Pyo had found the father of the enormous boy weeping before him. He’d found him in the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s uniform, surrounded by crows, and buried him with care.
And for the first time in his life, Sama Pyo had made a friend.
A friend more precious than family—the only person who cared for him more than his own father did.
But he’d never imagined he would make more friends over a decade later.
“Living with them taught me that, in the end, everything depends on the choices I make.”
The Fire Dragon Pavilion.
Despite its grand name, it had fewer than ten members. Among them, Sama Pyo had found a path he’d never known existed.
There were no shackles or labels there.
They always trusted one another and fought together, and that was how they overcame each crisis.
Perhaps that was why Sama Pyo had begun looking back on his life again and again.
Why, at some point, he had begun to feel something unfamiliar toward his merciless father.
“It occurred to me that, when you look at it, you’re rather pitiable yourself.”
“You probably weren’t like this from the start. Ambition took hold of you little by little. Then one day, you stopped caring what it took to get what you wanted.”
Gone was the son who couldn’t bear to meet his father’s cold gaze.
Now Sama Pyo looked at his dying father with calm, sorrowful eyes.
“It wasn’t a coincidence.”
“What... do you mean?”
“I didn’t come back by chance. I came to be with you at the end. Not as the Black Night King’s heir, but as Sima Gong’s son.”
Splash.
“Do you know?”
Sama Pyo sat in the pool of blood and met his father’s eyes. Watching them tremble, he continued slowly.
“There is no son in this world who can kill his father.”
“I’ll tell them everything myself. I’ll tell them about the pathetic son who knew of his father’s betrayal and tried not to see it.”
“I’m not asking to be forgiven. I’m choosing to bear it.”
There was such peace in his answer, such acceptance, that Sima Gong could say nothing.
He could only struggle to hold back a feeling he’d long forgotten—a feeling he had remembered only here, today.
His vision slowly darkened. His breathing grew short, as if signaling the end.
“You asked why I did it. Why I, who’d spent my whole life chasing survival and practical gain, made such a foolish choice...”
To save the heir who would inherit everything he had?
No. That wasn’t it.
At least in that moment, Sima Gong knew there had been another reason.
He was simply too late to confess it.
“I... This father of yours...”
Facing the son who had returned to be with him at the end, Sima Gong used all the strength he had left to force out the words.
He didn’t even realize they were his final breath.
Slump.
His head suddenly drooped.
To his father, who had died so wretchedly, as if burdened by the deeds of his life, the son whispered, “I heard you. Clearly.”
Sama Pyo’s shoulders began to shake. The pool of blood soaking father and son trembled with them.
Highly trained hunting dogs always obey their master’s commands.
They fix their eyes on the prey he points out, bare their teeth and growl. The moment he slips their leashes, they race forward and tear into it with all their strength.
Until their prey stops breathing.
Or until their master orders them to stop and return.
Just like now.
Shwaa!
A fierce, piercing whistle and a flash of light came from the side.
But speed was always relative.
The Sword Energy surged along a white blade and fell toward the top of my head with all the speed expected of a Peak Master. To me, though, it wasn’t fast.
Shhk!
Space split in an instant.
A fraction of a beat later came the slicing sound. Everything in the silver-white spearhead’s path had been cut apart.
The Sword Energy, snuffed out like a candle in the wind.
The blade that had carried that mighty energy.
And finally, the body of the person who had launched this futile attack.
Fwoosh!
A tremendous fountain of blood burst from his cleanly severed body. I didn’t blink at the sight.
Neither did the other hunting dogs charging from every direction, even now.
Thud, crunch! Whump!

I drove my spearhead into the chest of the first enemy charging straight at me, then crushed the face of another who came at me from the blind spot with one punch. At the same time, I yanked out the embedded spearhead and swung it.
“Ghk—kgh.”
Thump.
Three Peak Masters fell with dying cries in place of last words.
No—not three masters.
Three corpses.
But the frenzy of battle sweeping across the blood-soaked snowfield showed no sign of easing.
Shh-shh-shh-shhk!
The Dark Heaven cultists rushed in to fill the gaps without giving me a moment’s pause.
At the sight of their blank faces and eyes devoid of feeling, I felt an exhaustion so deep it weighed down my whole body.
How many is that now?
I had no idea.
I had neither the time nor the reason to count every enemy I’d killed.
I could only fight. Keep knocking them down.
Those soulless wooden puppets.
Those hunting dogs, those moths to the flame blindly carrying out their final order even though the master who held their leashes was gone.
Of course, I knew what this was.
A one-sided massacre. Slaughter.
But I had to do it.
It was the only way to end this blood-soaked battle, and the only way to save as many allies as possible.
So I had no choice but to cling with all my strength to the thread of consciousness that felt ready to snap at any moment.
Come on.
I muttered the words to myself and charged toward the enemy.
Or tried to.
That was when my vision began to fade.
A red alarm bell rang in my head.
My mental strength had reached its limit long ago. Now, unable to endure any longer, it was sending me a warning.
But by the time I gritted my teeth and forced my eyes wide, it was already too late.
Shwaa!
My view had tilted. A dozen blades were raining down on my body, which had staggered without my even realizing it.
They looked faint. Slow.
My eyesight was still sharp enough to follow them. The problem was my brain: the part that needed to tell my body to move had frozen like stone.
Damn it.
I cursed inwardly as the world slowed around me.
These men were no Blood-Sword Demon Lord or Grand Sorceress. They couldn’t even compare to the Black Ghosts.
They fell far short.
Under normal circumstances, I would’ve scoffed at the difference between us.
Even so, I had a gut feeling I wouldn’t be able to dodge all their attacks.
And while my body refused to move, one ridiculous thought crossed my mind.
If I level up, would it heal me even if my limbs got cut off?
Fortunately, I didn’t have to worry about that unpleasant first experience—the sort only someone like Cheongpung might enjoy.
The next moment, an enormous rush of air sounded from somewhere and swept my worries away.
Whoooosh!
It happened in the blink of an eye.
A huge shadow rose over the shoulders of the enemies charging toward me. With it came a two-section staff, big and beautiful just as its name suggested, cleaving through the air like lightning.
Craaaack!
If anyone ever asked whether I’d seen five heads knocked flying with a single swing of a bat, I could nod without hesitation.
I could even name the top prospect who’d tear through the modern Major Leagues, now a playground for Awakened Ones.
Of course, that lunatic hulk would introduce himself before anyone else got the chance.
Just like now.
“Taishan! Came! Saw! Hit!”
“Well done! Now, Body Slam!”
Starting with Namho, perched on the shoulder of Taishan—who had just delivered a line to make Julius Caesar weep—familiar faces burst onto the scene like streaks of light.
“Young Master! No, Benefactor! No, Pavilion Master!”
Shhk!
Ju Hwaran split an enemy’s skull while blurting out a three-step change of address that even Transformers would’ve had trouble keeping up with.
“Fools! You dare try to harm the Captain? Your courage is admirable, but first you’ll have to get past me—the Captain’s right arm and heart! I, Hyuk Mu—whoa, shit!”
Clang!
Hyuk Mujin had charged in with a grand entrance, only to scramble backward when his opponent’s counterattack proved stronger than he’d expected.
“Uh, does that guy know how to fight with his mouth shut?”
“You should try shutting yours first.”
Thrust!
Song Ilseom saved Hyuk Mujin and cut down the remaining enemies in a flash. And... wait, who was that black, shaggy old guy?
“The Seven Masters of the Black Horse?”
The name slipped out before I knew it. The middle-aged man, a former mounted bandit, twisted his already fearsome face.
“Not Black Horse—White Horse! I’m Ma Junggeol, eldest of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang! Who do you think I went through all this shit for? And you forgot me...!”
“Lower your voice. While I’m asking nicely.”
At Ju Hwaran’s chilling warning, Ma Junggeol clamped his mouth shut. A laugh escaped me before I knew it.
It was just good to see them.
To know we hadn’t lost anyone.
And...
Because I could see the one last person I’d thought I’d never meet again.
“You made it?”
Sama Pyo, who I hadn’t even seen arrive, shrugged.
“Am I late?”
No.
Not at all.
