“I doubt he’s a spy.”
“It’s true that he led the horse caravans of Ningxia Province to help our side.
But we mustn’t trust him completely.
You know that as well as I do, don’t you?”
Of course I did.
I’d been stabbed in the back often enough to be sick of it.
First the Head Elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, then even the Murong Family, one of the Five Great Families, had joined forces with Dark Heaven.
Blindly trusting some unidentified Supreme Peak master who’d crawled out of who-knows-where would be stupid.
But...
“There’s no reason we can’t trust him if we have enough evidence.”
“Evidence?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s question, I barely moved my lips.
“System.”
The brief Sound Transmission reached his ear, and his eyes widened.
I’d already told Jeok Cheongang what the System was, though the word meant nothing in this world.
He lowered his voice.
“So what has that marvelous ability of yours told you?”
“He’s mad.
Thoroughly mad.”
“Meaning he isn’t a spy?”
“Yes.
I can’t say it with absolute certainty, though.”
“If you had to put a number on it?”
“Ninety-nine point nine percent.
That’s the chance the madman—no, Great Sir—isn’t a spy.”
“Great Sir, my ass.
He’s a lunatic.”
Jeok Cheongang frowned slightly and smacked his lips.
“You’re suspicious of everything, though it doesn’t suit you.
If you’re saying this, you must be all but certain...
So you think he truly suffers from madness?”
I hesitated, then nodded.
Even I, who thought I had a pretty good grasp of most of the System, had never encountered anything like this.
I couldn’t be a hundred percent sure, but otherwise, there was no explaining why Great Sir’s name kept changing from one moment to the next.
At least he isn’t lying.
Fooling the System is practically impossible, no matter what you try.
That left only one answer.
Gaettong, Sottong, Malttong, Jeomsuni—whatever the name, Great Sir firmly believed it was his, and the System reflected that belief.
In the purest sense of the word, he was mad.
“He’s dressed so badly that Myriad-Mile Pursuit, that head beggar, would weep.
But he doesn’t look old enough to be suffering from the infirmities of old age...
I haven’t the faintest idea where that stray cur came from.”
Jeok Cheongang had casually reduced the Beggars’ Sect Leader to “that head beggar.” He frowned, but even he had little chance of working out Great Sir’s identity on the spot.
Too many people remained hidden across the vast Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes, the Four Seas and Five Lakes.
Eccentrics in remote mountain valleys, far from the rest of the world.
Heirs of secret sects who had chosen to be forgotten.
Fugitives and killers living quietly out of sight somewhere.
Jeok Cheongang himself had stayed shut away on Mount Jiuhua until he was nearly sixty, devoting himself entirely to martial arts.
Great Sir might well be someone like him.
In fact, quite a few reclusive masters had joined the Murim Alliance since it was newly founded at the Mount Song Resolution.
Unlike Great Sir, of course, they must have been thoroughly vetted.
The Murim Alliance wasn’t a college club.
This was wartime, with betrayal and intrigue everywhere.
But how should I put it?
A sudden conviction came over me, and before I knew it, I’d spoken aloud.
“Let’s take him in as an ally.”
“What?”
“Like I said, I don’t think Great Sir is a Dark Heaven spy.
No—I’m sure he isn’t.”
Jeok Cheongang looked at me in surprise.
I sounded more certain than usual.
“Well, that’s strange.
What makes you trust that suspicious madman so much?”
“That’s...”
I let the words trail off.
Honestly, I didn’t know.
The System didn’t tell me who was friend or foe.
But alongside my curiosity about Great Sir, I felt a strangely strong conviction that this unidentified Supreme Peak master was not our enemy.
I couldn’t give a reason for it, even to myself.
...Maybe I’m just exhausted.
As soon as I remembered how tired I was, my vision wavered.
I looked around.
After half a day of fighting, the snowfield was covered in blood and bodies.
People were clearing the battlefield, the brief joy of victory already forgotten.
Birds had gathered in a black mass overhead, circling in the air.
Dark clouds hid the sky.
The ground beneath them was red.
Through my wavering vision, it looked like a future that would repeat forever.
“Did we... really win?”
My voice came out faint.
Jeok Cheongang answered.
“Yes.
At least for today.”
But why?
Why, after defeating more enemies than I could count, saving so many lives, and finally winning a great victory that had kept Gansu Province safe—
Why, when I was still alive and breathing—
It didn’t feel like we’d won.
I wasn’t happy at all.
Not even when a clear chime rang in my ears.
Ding, ding, ding.
System Quest conditions have been met.
Mission: Eliminate all enemies in the Gansu Province area (Complete).
Quest Path of Blood successfully completed.
You have acquired a massive amount of EXP and Fame.
A new chain Quest has been created.
Would you like to check the updated information?
Y / N
I suddenly lifted my head.
Beyond the translucent holographic window, pitch-black clouds still hid the sky.
I took a deep breath, and the air that sank deep into my body reeked of blood.
When would I finally be free of this sight?
How much more would I have to suffer, how many more deaths would I have to watch, before I could escape this horrible cycle?
But as always, I had no choice but to answer.
Accept.
It had been a cruel fucking day.
Crack.
Crunch.
Beyond the faintly flickering candlelight, a pair of eyes watched a writhing shadow in silence as the gruesome sounds of tearing flesh filled the room.
At first glance, the eyes seemed so deeply sunk that it was impossible to guess what lay behind them.
Even so, they held a trace of contempt and disgust—and that look remained even after the tearing sounds stopped.
The shadow’s convulsions gradually subsided.
At last, it rose and immediately voiced its displeasure.
“You bitch.
What’s with that look?”
It was a rough greeting after so long apart, but the woman paid it little mind.
She had always prided herself on being rational.
She knew better than to expect a mere beast to show human courtesy.
That didn’t mean she had anything kind to say to it.
“Wipe yourself off.
And stop stinking up the place.”
“What?
I stink?”
At the woman’s sharp words, the shadow started to reply, then gave a quiet laugh.
“Fine.
I’ll do as I’m told.
You’re already in a bad mood, aren’t you?”
“...What nonsense are you talking about now?”
“Don’t pretend you don’t know when it doesn’t suit you.
Don’t.
It makes you look pathetic.”
Swish.
Cloth slid over smooth muscle and skin.
In the darkness beyond the candlelight, the shadow wiped the blood from its body and spoke.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
“I heard you nearly failed...
So, how was it, you miserable bitch?
You mocked me last time, but it wasn’t so easy when you had to face him yourself, was it?”
The Grand Sorceress silently bit her lip.
She had little room to argue.
It was the truth.
When her silence dragged on, the shadow laughed aloud and continued.
“You should’ve been much more careful.
I don’t care if you die, but you nearly caused a serious setback to the grand plan.”
The Grand Sorceress frowned at the continuing taunts and shot back.
“The same goes for you.”
“Isn’t it embarrassing to compare this with what happened then?
I caused a bloodbath in the heart of the Central Plains with just a handful of idiots.
Even squinting, you can see these are different matters.”
Step.
The shadow—no, the Blood Lord—chuckled as if to mock her, then stepped into the faint light.
“And I had an important item to secure on top of that.”
He had not shown himself since the Shaolin Bloodshed that shook the whole world.
Now he crossed the spacious room with a jaunty stride.
He sat in a grand chair that bore the marks of centuries and gave off an inexplicable air of authority.
Propping his chin on one hand, he gazed at the Grand Sorceress.
As if he were the ruler of a kingdom.
“Well, enough about the past.
What matters is the present and the future.
Don’t you agree?”
This time, the Grand Sorceress gave a quiet laugh.
She shook her head and stared at the Blood Lord sitting in the grand chair.
“Stop talking as if you’re someone important.
You’re a stupid beast.
No—a monster.”
“A monster, huh?
To the people of the Central Plains, aren’t we as bad as each other?”
“No.
Serving that person is the only thing we have in common.
None of us is like you.”
Despite the contempt in her voice, the Blood Lord merely shrugged.
“True.
That’s the first thing you’ve got right.”
“...What?”
The Grand Sorceress was taken aback by the response, which was nothing like what she’d expected.
A smile, deep as blood, spread across the Blood Lord’s lips.
“Of course none of you is like me.
No one—not even you—has ever achieved as much as I have.”
He laughed gleefully and stroked the grand chair.
More precisely, he stroked the two characters carved into part of it in a bold, vigorous hand.
Kunlun.
A whirling snowstorm swept past the jagged mountain peaks and crept into the Taiqing Hall, where the two of them faced each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 1063
paragraphs: People say that a rumor without feet can travel a thousand li, while information with wings can reach tens of thousands of li away.
The information merchants of Murim held that saying up as a proverb, and it was no exaggeration.
Flap!
On the day dark clouds covered the sky and death claimed the land, dozens of messenger eagles took flight at once. It was quite a sight.
They left mountains of corpses and pools of blood behind, soaring high and beating their great wings toward separate destinations.
The red-stained snowfield shrank to a tiny drop of blood. The Great Snow Mountain Range, blanketed in eternal snow, disappeared from view.
The sun and moon traded places several times. Day gave way to night and night to day, until the ocher plateau that seemed to stretch to the ends of the world vanished beyond the horizon.
And at last, when the dozens of messenger eagles had each completed their journeys, the realm of the Central Plains seethed like lava in a crater.
“Waaaaah!”
“Long live the Great Nation! Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
“What are you all doing? Come out! Hurry!”
The news reached different places at different times, but wherever people heard what had happened in Gansu Province, they rushed into the streets and cheered.
Even those roused from a sound sleep before dawn came out of their houses more bewildered than angry.
“Which goddamn fools are making a racket at this hour, when even the hens are fast asleep... Hey, you lot! What the hell are you doing carrying on in front of someone else’s house?”
On an ordinary day, sharp words like those would probably have led to people grabbing each other by the collars first and asking questions later.
But the crowd was too excited. Cheering loud enough to chase away the predawn darkness, they shouted back again and again.
“A great victory! A great victory!”
“What nonsense is that? I asked what you’re doing—wait. A great victory?”
“Good heavens, look at you. You haven’t heard the news yet, have you?”
“You haven’t heard? The rebels from Xinjiang invaded Gansu without knowing their place, and got wiped out to the last man!”
“What? They went after Gansu?”
Only then did the newcomers’ eyes widen. Highborn or lowborn, their shock was the same.
How could it not be?
Just a year ago, Dark Heaven was a name heard only among those with sharp eyes and ears. Now even a peasant scraping out a living in a remote village knew who they were.
The rebels of Xinjiang. Fiends from beyond the desert.
Even the Demonic Cult, which had unleashed the bloodshed known as the Great Faction War half a century ago, could not match Dark Heaven’s infamy today.
The Demonic Cult of old had sought to conquer the Murim of the Central Plains. Dark Heaven sought to claim the world itself.
Defying heaven.
Those two characters said it all. Dark Heaven would overturn heaven, defy the natural order, and destroy the unified dynasty and the peace won after countless ages of turmoil.
That was Dark Heaven. And so the people of the Great Nation were still roaming the streets, cheering at that very moment.
“Good heavens, what wonderful news. But just how great a victory was it to get everyone worked up like this?”
At the question, which came from someone now thoroughly awake, a proud voice rose from the crowd.
“Don’t be shocked. From what I hear, tens of thousands of rebels were killed or captured in a single battle.”
“Gasp! Tens of thousands!”

The numbers were staggering—far beyond those of a mere cult—and so was the victory they represented. They had barely caught their breath when voices elsewhere in the crowd rose to contradict the claim.
“What nonsense! A martial artist I know told me they wiped out a hundred thousand in half a day.”
“A hundred thousand? Wasn’t it three hundred thousand?”
“What are you all talking about? I heard they crushed more than a million rebels!”
“Come on. There’s a limit to how much nonsense a man can talk. A million?”
“Then let’s split the difference and call it half a million. No, three hundred thousand.”
“Three hundred thousand is still too many. Where did you hear that?”
“Are you with Dark Heaven? Can’t you read the room?”
“Why has this suddenly become about—”
“So, are we going with three hundred thousand or not?”
“...Is that up to me?”
“Ah, three hundred thousand! Just so you know, I’m not budging any further!”
“A-all right. I’ll remember it as three hundred thousand. Just calm down.”
“Now we’re getting somewhere. Repeat after me: Long live the Great Nation!”
“L-long live the Great Nation.”
“Speak up! I can barely hear you!”
“L-long live!”
“Much better. Now, long live the Murim Alliance!”
“...When does this end?”
“We’re not done yet. After that comes long live the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—no, the Marquis of Shangshan. Be ready.”
A few people were less than enthusiastic, but most common folk cheered the Murim Alliance just as freely.
It was a remarkable change in public opinion, even compared with only a few years ago.
The orthodox faction, led by the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, had ruled the Murim of the Central Plains. But a long peace had brought corruption, and power had bred injustice.
Did wearing spotless white make the heart beneath it white too?
Still water eventually went foul. Perfect good and perfect evil existed nowhere.
But things were different now.
“Long live the Marquis of Shangshan!”
“Long live the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
It was hard not to marvel at how much had changed because of one man.
Jin Taekyung.
His path, which had begun about two years ago, was as deep and immense as the footsteps of a giant.

The Jin Family of Taiyuan, once slowly crumbling, had become a power that ruled beyond Shanxi Province and across the northern grasslands. It had even joined the Five Great Families. And that was only a fraction of what he had achieved.

Jin Taekyung was the heir of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, and the successor to the Fire Gate Clan. He was the young giant who had raised the banner of a new Murim Alliance alongside Murim’s most renowned leaders. With martial prowess scarcely believable for his age, he fought Dark Heaven as a man of righteousness.
There was no martial artist under heaven who did not know his name.
No one doubted or begrudged the meaning and weight of the four characters Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
No. No one dared.
Jin Taekyung had proven himself, and countless people had seen it happen.
Nor was his standing confined within Murim’s iron fence.
“To all the people under heaven, hear this!”
The Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven, the great ruler who governed the land on heaven’s behalf, had proclaimed his mandate to the world.

The Emperor revealed every scheme Dark Heaven had carried out. He named his only surviving younger brother Imperial Younger Brother and heir apparent, declared the fiends beyond the desert traitors, and tore down in one stroke the solid wall that had stood between the government and Murim for ages.
His battering ram was none other than Jin Taekyung, the Marquis of Shangshan.
“By the command of the Son of Heaven, I order you: unite and fight! Protect your land from the rebels with supernatural powers who dare defy the natural order!”
And so the name Jin Taekyung resounded beyond Murim, echoing across the Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes, the Four Seas and Five Lakes.

To martial artists, he was the young giant who would lead a new era. To countless common folk, he was the guardian of the imperial court, the Great General of the realm who obeyed the Emperor’s solemn command and put down traitors.
A martial artist and, at the same time, a marquis personally appointed by the Emperor.
Nothing like it had ever happened in the Great Nation’s history—or anywhere else’s. Yet it was real, and the young hero fought at every moment to bring this terrible age of chaos to an end.
Now he had won again.
“Waaaaah!”
“The Great Nation and Murim have finally united to drive out the rebels! Isn’t it all thanks to His Majesty’s reign and the Marquis of Shangshan’s efforts?”
“On a day like this, there’s no way I’m not getting drunk. Bring me a jar of wine! No—three jars!”
The story swelled as it passed from mouth to mouth. Even without the embellishments, the victory was beyond dispute.
Taverns filled to capacity, and the revelers spilled into the streets, happily raising their cups with the victory in Gansu as their reason to drink.

They praised the Emperor, thanked Jin Taekyung and the Murim Alliance for risking their lives to protect the people of the realm, and took comfort in knowing that they and their loved ones were safe because of them.
They let themselves hope, however vaguely, that the war might soon end without much harm to anyone.
“Come on, drink! Hurry!”
“Down the hatch! That’s it!”
Laughter rang out everywhere. Amid the great feasts, there was not a trace of fear on anyone’s face.
Martial artists and common folk alike laughed aloud and reveled in their victory.
For that one day, at least.
Until a peregrine falcon from the distant western frontier of Qinghai completed its weary journey.
When I was a kid, I used to be really disappointed if I couldn’t remember a dream from the night before.
It must’ve been an exciting story, too.
But somewhere along the way, I learned that forgetting a dream meant I wouldn’t have to shudder at the feeling a nightmare left behind.
Of course, it didn’t mean I hadn’t had the nightmare.
“Here.”
I opened my eyes on a swaying saddle to find Hyuk Mujin’s face in front of me. He was holding out a piece of cloth.
“...What’s this?”
“What do you think? Take it. I can’t wipe you down myself.”
“Oh.”
Only then did I feel my clothes clinging to me from head to toe. What the hell had I dreamed about to break out in this much cold sweat?
I know.
Since becoming a Hunter, my nightmares had usually featured one of two kinds of people.
People who’d died because I couldn’t save them.
Or people who’d died by my hand.
Actually, there’s been one more recently, for the first time in a while.
I remembered it suddenly.
A strange, unidentifiable dream.
Memories that could never have belonged to me, Jin Taekyung of Korea. Memories of a past lived by Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I was wondering if the dream I’d just had had been like those when—
Screee!
A bird cried out somewhere above me, breaking my train of thought.
As if telling me to focus on the present instead of a dream that might as well have been an illusion.
Right. Now’s not the time.
I gave my head a small shake and drew up the Scorching Yang Qi within me.
Whoosh. Crackle.
Steam billowed out, and my damp clothes dried in an instant. Hyuk Mujin’s face flushed from the gentle warmth, and he muttered in a dazed voice:
“...Oh. Right. There’s that way too.”
“Sure. Unlike you.”
“...Are you showing off?”
“Yeah.”
“Well, when you admit it like that, there’s not much I can say...”
Hyuk Mujin let his words trail off, still not quite satisfied. At that moment—
Screee!
The cry rang out again. I looked up at the sky without thinking.
My eyes widened.
A blood-soaked missive was tied to the leg of a falcon gliding overhead, its great wings spread wide.

People who’d died because I couldn’t save them.
Or people who’d died by my hand.
Actually, there’s been one more recently, for the first time in a while.
I remembered it suddenly.
A strange, unidentifiable dream.
Memories that could never have belonged to me, Jin Taekyung of Korea.
Memories of a past lived by Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I was wondering if the dream I’d just had had been like those when—
Screee!
A bird cried out somewhere above me, breaking my train of thought.
As if telling me to focus on the present instead of a dream that might as well have been an illusion.
Right.
Now’s not the time.
I gave my head a small shake and drew up the Scorching Yang Qi within me.
Whoosh.
Crackle.
Steam billowed out, and my damp clothes dried in an instant.
Hyuk Mujin’s face flushed from the gentle warmth, and he muttered in a dazed voice:
Right.
There’s that way too.”
“Sure.
Unlike you.”
“...Are you showing off?”
“Yeah.”
“Well, when you admit it like that, there’s not much I can say...”
Hyuk Mujin let his words trail off, still not quite satisfied.
At that moment—
Screee!
The cry rang out again.
I looked up at the sky without thinking.
My eyes widened.
A blood-soaked missive was tied to the leg of a falcon gliding overhead, its great wings spread wide.

chapters.title: Chapter 1064
paragraphs: If they’d spotted it even a little later, the messenger eagle would have flown right over everyone’s heads.
Even messenger eagles, raised with far more rigorous training and care than messenger pigeons, were only trained to fly between set destinations.
But a handful of people, Jin Taekyung among them, noticed it just in time. The Bow Saint was one of them.
When it came to archery, she was the greatest under heaven—perhaps even the greatest in all history.
Shing. Clack.
It happened in an instant.
Steel joints locked together with a metallic clack, transforming her two strangely curved swords into a bow. The Bow Saint drew the string without hesitation.
“Now!”
At Jin Taekyung’s shout, she released the taut bowstring.
Boom!
The air tore apart.
A streak of light shot faster than sound and reached the messenger eagle, a distant speck in the sky, in the blink of an eye.
Jin Taekyung, who had anticipated all of this, shot forward at the same moment.
Whoooosh!
He surged ahead like a gust of wind.
In a single bound, he crossed dozens of jang and caught the falling eagle, an arrow through its wing.
Peep. Peep.
“Spit on it and it’ll heal in no time, you idiot.”
Despite his gruff words, Jin Taekyung stroked the mournfully crying eagle’s beak. Then he hurriedly checked its leg.
This is...
He swallowed a groan. A missive had been rolled into a tight little bundle and fastened around the eagle’s leg.
Foreboding struck before he’d even read it.
There was no doubt about the reddish substance smeared across the missive. It was blood, spilled from someone’s body.
And in his experience, a premonition like this had never been wrong.
Kunlun fallen.
The moment Jin Taekyung read the first line of the missive, scrawled in a rough hand, he bit down on his lip without realizing it.
The Kunlun Mountains.
This immense range at the western edge of Qinghai held an ancient history and countless legends.
Its ridges stretched for thousands of jang, reaching plateaus and deserts. Its peaks rose high enough to deserve the name of the highest summits.

But the Kunlun Mountains held particular significance for the martial artists of the realm for another reason—one every bit as important as the Kunlun Sect, birthplace of Daoist martial arts and heir to a long history.
“So the pass we had to hold has been breached.”
Jeok Cheongang spat out the words. The missive, already passed through several hands, was crumpled in his fist.
“If what’s written here is true and they’ve occupied Kunlun, then we’ve effectively lost half of Qinghai.”
At his low words, everyone nodded, their faces grim.

Jeok Cheongang was right. Most of the area around the Kunlun Mountains consisted of basins, and that vast region covered nearly half of Qinghai Province. If the enemy held it, the allies had lost control of it.
“Must bring back old memories. Doesn’t it, you old hag?”
The Bow Saint frowned at Jeok Cheongang’s sudden question.
“That’s not something I want to hear from you. Whether you mean my age or the unpleasant memories of the Great Faction War.”
“So how was it at the start of the Great Faction War? When those Demonic Cult bastards crossed Kunlun.”

“It was an unexpected attack. The Demonic Cult’s last invasion before the Great Faction War had been hundreds of years earlier, and even then they’d been soundly defeated before they could cross the Kunlun Mountains. So of course we never expected it.”
But people always fixated on what they couldn’t have.
The Heavenly Demon, who had built the Demonic Cult into a force stronger than ever some fifty years ago, was no exception.
“How many days did the Kunlun Sect hold out back then?”
“Three. They fought for exactly three days and nights before they could hold out no longer and retreated. Their losses nearly destroyed them.”
“Three days against a hundred thousand Demonic Cult bastards. They held out a long time.”
He wasn’t mocking them.
The Kunlun Sect had always accepted only a small number of Disciples because of its difficult location and strict rules. It had the fewest Disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang.

Yet its Disciples were formidable, and the Kunlun Mountains were more treacherous than even the Great Snow Mountain. Together, those advantages had let the sect repel the Demonic Cult’s invasions time and again.
Even so, the Kunlun Sect had its limits.
During the Great Faction War half a century ago.
And now.
The difference was that this time, unlike in the last Great Faction War, when the Demonic Cult dealt the Kunlun Sect a devastating blow as soon as hostilities began, they had made a wiser choice.
“At least they decided to retreat right away. Isn’t that right?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s sudden question, I nodded. I’d been lost in thought.
“Even I think that was the best choice. Facing them head-on would’ve been insane.”
The Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven were different in kind.
I wasn’t talking about the quality or number of their troops. The darkness within Dark Heaven was far deeper and more boundless than anyone could imagine.
Even I couldn’t begin to guess its true size or depth.
But one thing was certain.
“If they’d decided to fight to the death like they did during the Great Faction War, the Kunlun Sect would already have been erased from the world.”
Maybe the Kunlun Sect had realized the battle was hopeless, too.
That would explain why they’d retreated so quickly despite having been joined by Qinghai’s martial artists and government troops—a combined force of some twenty thousand.
The missive said around a thousand people had been killed or wounded during the retreat, but that didn’t change the fact that retreat had been their best choice.
“Fortunately, they withdrew to Qinghai Lake with most of their forces intact. We haven’t lost all of Qinghai yet.”
Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, had spoken up. I immediately shook my head.
“You’re not wrong, but at this rate, it’s only a matter of time. The forces left in Qinghai can’t hold them back.”
“That’s...”
“They have magic—no, dark arts with power that’s hard to believe. And the Dark Heaven forces occupying the Kunlun Mountains are too numerous to count.”
That wasn’t a figure of speech or an exaggeration.
I was only repeating what was written in the missive carried by the messenger eagle I’d just caught.
In the missive sent when the decision to retreat was made, a Kunlun Sect Elder had written:
Enemies too numerous to count were filling the mountains and advancing toward them.
At the sight of that overwhelming, terrifying force, he had found himself thinking of a day decades ago.
“...The Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples.”
The groan slipped from someone’s lips, and the air grew heavy. It was only natural.
Most of those present had already seen it with their own eyes.
They’d felt it on their skin, in every part of their bodies.
Most of the people here had seen and experienced Dark Heaven wield supernatural powers.
They must have felt despair and defeat as they watched a sight that tore down every assumption they’d ever held.
And now there were a hundred thousand.
Even if fear had gripped the Elder who wrote the missive, an army that brought the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples to mind couldn’t be far off in size.
And someone I know is probably among them.
Though we’d met only briefly, one unforgettable face passed before my eyes.
The Grand Mage.
No—the Grand Sorceress.
I couldn’t be certain, but I felt it in my gut. She had survived, and if she had, she would be in Qinghai by now.
If Qinghai falls, there’ll be no containing this.
Not just because it was Qinghai. Gansu, which we’d barely managed to protect, was in much the same position.
The realm was one enormous dam. A small crack, and the gap it opened, could bring the whole thing down.
We need time. Time to find a better way to stop them without taking even greater losses.
A headache came on.
But once again, time wasn’t on my side.
Or rather, not time. The System.
Logout.
I carefully repeated the word in my mind, holding on to a sliver of hope.
The System’s answer was calm and cold.
Beep.
System Logout is unavailable.
“...Damn it.”
Everyone’s attention snapped to me at the curse that escaped on instinct, but I didn’t care.
No. The situation was so fucked I couldn’t spare a thought for their stares.
Why?
I’d already spent months in Murim and faced death several times over.
But at some point, the System had shut the door tight and refused to open it.
It blocked my only way back to the modern world, forcing new Quests and a brutal reality on me instead.
Just as it had a few days ago, when we’d finally brought the long, cruel battle at the Great Snow Mountain to an end.
Just as it was doing now.
System The ongoing linked Quest, To Qinghai, has not yet been completed!
Crack.
I stared at the holographic window floating before me and swallowed the curse that sprang to my lips.

And, in a stroke of good luck amid all this misfortune, I cursed the System for tossing me a clue like alms in the form of a new Quest title. Then I spoke to a certain lunatic, who was the only one there nodding off like a sick chicken in the middle of this dire situation.
“You said you’d guide us, right?”
“Huh? Yeah?”
Only then did Great Sir blink blearily awake. He wiped the drool from his mouth and spoke in a sleepy voice.
“I think I did say that... So, have you decided where you’re going?”
“Yes.”
I straightened my back and looked around.
We had all paused here, in the Qilian Mountains. After several days of travel, we’d reached the far end of the range, where a new land awaited us.
Qinghai. Strange and dangerous.
“Let’s go.”
At my quiet words, everyone’s eyes lit up, and they rose to their feet.

chapters.title: Chapter 1065
paragraphs: Losing a battle meant the end.
Especially in a large-scale engagement, with tens of thousands clashing head-on.
The survivors on the losing side had only two possible fates: become prisoners or run to the ends of the earth.
They couldn’t choose between them. They couldn’t refuse them.
The victors were different.
So, three days ago, just after the bloody battle around the Great Snow Mountain ended in a crushing victory for our side, we were given a new choice.
Would we deal with the aftermath and stay to protect Gansu Province? Or would we move to stop the Dark Heaven forces advancing somewhere else?
We chose the latter.
No—more accurately, everyone respected my wishes.
“I’ll be leaving now. There’s something I have to do.”
The snowfield was covered in flames and smoke that day.

The fire, consuming tens of thousands of corpses, burned as if it would never go out. And my sudden announcement must have felt unbearably cruel to those watching the scene, their tears falling without end.
Yet even though I’d denied them the time to grieve, they didn’t blame me.
Not one of them.
Only Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, the Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, stepped forward with a question.
“Where do you intend to go?”
My answer had been decided from the start.
The System had already pointed the way to our next destination with a Quest as clear as a compass.
“Qinghai. Qinghai.”
“Which means...”
“Yes. They’re coming.”
I spoke with a certainty I couldn’t explain, but Perfected Being Hyeoncheon didn’t ask why. He only nodded, his expression grave.
“The world will be stained with blood once more.”
“It will. Without a doubt.”
“If we win another great victory against them there, do you think we can bring this accursed war to an end?”
“We’ll be one step closer. And the step we take this time will be bigger and deeper than any before it.”
“Deep enough to reach the Lord of Heaven?”
“I believe so.”
“Then the Kongtong Sect will stand with you.”
“We won’t stop until we reach the end. If only for the sake of the souls who must now be under the care of the Primordial Heavenly Venerable, beyond those clouds.”
If Perfected Being Hyeoncheon had been giving off the same killing intent he’d shown while slaughtering the surviving Dark Heaven followers, I would have refused his offer.
But the old Daoist had lost so much, and his eyes were clear. The same was true of the Kongtong Disciples, who had poured out their anger and grief.
“All right.”
And so Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and about a hundred Kongtong Disciples joined us. But that was only the beginning.
“I, Hyuk Sopyung, a junior martial artist, humbly ask leave to answer for my sect’s sins.”
Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.
Along with him, more than three hundred Zhongnan Sect Disciples who had barely survived the bloody battle set down their weapons and knelt.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom.
The two elders of their sect were dead, and now the Disciples knew what they had done. Shame and grief filled their faces. Blood trickled between their tightly clenched teeth.
If the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, the Zhongnan Sect Leader, hadn’t been unconscious from his severe injuries, he would have knelt beside them and asked to answer for those sins too.
Perfected Being Hyeoncheon watched the Zhongnan Disciples in silence for a long while. Then he spoke.
“A father’s sins do not belong to his children, nor a master’s to his Disciples. Why, then, do the Disciples of Zhongnan ask me to hold them to account?”
“Still, if you insist on accepting a penalty, so be it. Follow Daoist Friend Jin here and walk a straight, honorable path. Let that be the Zhongnan Sect’s new way.”
At the old Daoist’s wise and compassionate words, Hyuk Sopyung and the Zhongnan Disciples bowed deeply. Then they gave me a fist-and-palm salute with the utmost respect.
“We wish to walk the righteous path without straying an inch. Great Hero Jin, we ask to join you.”
It was the first time I’d come face-to-face with Hyuk Sopyung since the incident at the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
He had once been the Zhongnan Sect’s most promising young prodigy, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes. The gap between us had grown even wider than before.

Even after spending several days alongside the Zhongnan Sect in Gansu, I’d only ever passed him at a distance. Maybe that was why I’d only just noticed how much more serious his bearing had become, how much deeper his gaze.
“I’d be glad to have you.”
For once, I accepted an offer with proper courtesy. Our numbers had swelled to around five hundred with the two sects joining us, and someone watching it all came over.
“Even this won’t be enough. Don’t you think?”
“Maybe. Still better than padding our numbers with any old riffraff.”
“Funny. My ears are itching. Must be my imagination.”
“Maybe not.”
The new Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate gave a dry laugh at my feigned innocence, then pointed to his new followers, lined up in orderly ranks.

“Five hundred. Time was short, but I chose them carefully from the volunteers. They may not measure up to the Disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but I can vouch for their loyalty and fighting spirit.”
“So you’re putting them under my command?”
“No. I’d be grateful if you let them come with you.”
“What?”

“I, Sama Pyo, Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, and five hundred men ask to join the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. Please allow us to fight for the realm and make up, however little, for our past wrongs.”
For a moment, I couldn’t speak.
I might not have been able to hold back the emotion welling up inside me if a giant with a little old man dangling from his neck hadn’t shouted right then.
“Taishan’s going! Taishan’s going too! Taishan will go with the Pavilion Master to the end!”
“Goddamn it! Stop bouncing around so much! Please!”
Everyone burst out laughing at once, as if they’d planned it.
Me, Sama Pyo, the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, and the survivors of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Even Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, whose expression never changed whether he was happy or sad.
“You martial artists are quite an amusing lot.”
“Really? Since you brought it up, want to hear something even funnier?”
“Something funnier?”

“Yeah. It’s about a certain Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who kept talking back to a Marquis like he was his equal and is now on the verge of being forcibly discharged. The funny thing is, he has the same surname as you. What a coincidence, huh?”
“...Is that how you’re going to play this?”
“Then do your best. So I don’t have to.”
Jeong Hogun shook his head as though there was no winning with me. Then he stood as straight as an iron tower and saluted.
“Then please give your orders.”
“Qinghai. We’re going to Qinghai Province. At full speed.”
“I, Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, accept the solemn order of the Most Honorable Marquis of Shangshan.”
And so, two days ago, the Embroidered Uniform Guard joined us as the final piece of our force. Now nearly two thousand strong, we took a brief rest and headed straight for Qinghai Province.
A few people raised the cautious possibility that Dark Heaven might target Gansu again. The Bow Saint put those concerns to rest with a single remark.
“The North is moving.”
Naturally, she didn’t mean northern Gansu.
She meant the North of the entire world, divided by the Great Wall—and the two powers that ruled that vast land.
The fierce tiger of Hebei: the Hebei Peng Family.
And the Azure Dragon of Shanxi Province: the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who had now claimed even the skies above the green grasslands.
“Arrows may fly at different speeds, but so long as they hold their course, each will eventually strike its target.”
The Bow Saint and the Embroidered Uniform Guard, for example, were arrows shot ahead of the rest.
It was a metaphor worthy of the Bow Saint. No one argued after that.
Not merely because she was the Bow Saint. Everyone knew that with the Azure Dragon and the fierce tiger of the North spreading their wings and baring their claws, Gansu was reasonably safe.
And the brief purge just before we left Gansu was enough to wipe out any possible future threat.
“Anything you want to say before you die? Spare me the excuses. I’ll hear your last words.”
“I—I never colluded with Dark Heaven. There must have been some misunderstanding!”
“Young Sect Leader—no, Sect Leader! Why are you doing this? You know your late father and I were practically sworn brothers!”
“Yeah, I know. Close enough to betray us together. You were so close that my father wrote it all down in detail... Did you know that?”
The meeting meant to decide the future of Gansu’s Murim had become a trial of its traitors. The room froze.
Wide eyes. Trembling lips.
Sama Pyo gave a quiet sigh at the sight of them, took a battered old book from inside his robe, and set it on the table.
“So you didn’t know. I’d have thought you might at least suspect.”
Even I was surprised that the meticulous Black Night King, Sima Gong, had left such conclusive evidence behind. How much more shocked must those men have been, after knowing him for decades?
Sama Pyo went on. There was a trace of bitterness toward his father in his voice, and he looked at the men as though they were insects.
“So. Any last words?”
That did it.
“You—you little brat, with the blood barely dry on your head! You dare kill me, your uncle in all but name?!”
“Heh. Heh heh. So this is how it ends.”
A cornered rat had only two choices.
Charge with its adorable little front teeth as its only weapon, or give up and accept its fate.
And waiting for the fools who chose to charge was—
“Story’s over, Taishan.”

Taishan’s two-section staff was gleefully spitting fire—no, blood.

“How could you do what you did, Sect Leader?”

“Shut your filthy mouth.”
“What?”

“What are the members of the Lanzhou Hyuk Family doing?!”
“Please don’t hold it against us, Family Head. You were the one who betrayed us first.”
“Y-you dare...!”

“Ma Junggeol told me he does, anyway. I don’t know what he did when he was young, but apparently he knows the terrain inside out.”

“Fucking hell.”

Step.

sentences.text: Losing a battle meant the end.
Especially in a large-scale engagement, with tens of thousands clashing head-on.
The survivors on the losing side had only two possible fates: become prisoners or run to the ends of the earth.
They couldn’t choose between them.
They couldn’t refuse them.
The victors were different.
So, three days ago, just after the bloody battle around the Great Snow Mountain ended in a crushing victory for our side, we were given a new choice.
Would we deal with the aftermath and stay to protect Gansu Province?
Or would we move to stop the Dark Heaven forces advancing somewhere else?
We chose the latter.
No—more accurately, everyone respected my wishes.
“I’ll be leaving now.
There’s something I have to do.”
The snowfield was covered in flames and smoke that day.
The fire, consuming tens of thousands of corpses, burned as if it would never go out.
And my sudden announcement must have felt unbearably cruel to those watching the scene, their tears falling without end.
Yet even though I’d denied them the time to grieve, they didn’t blame me.
Not one of them.
Only Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, the Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, stepped forward with a question.
“Where do you intend to go?”
My answer had been decided from the start.
The System had already pointed the way to our next destination with a Quest as clear as a compass.
“Qinghai.
Qinghai.”
“Which means...”
“Yes.
They’re coming.”
I spoke with a certainty I couldn’t explain, but Perfected Being Hyeoncheon didn’t ask why.
He only nodded, his expression grave.
“The world will be stained with blood once more.”
“It will.
Without a doubt.”
“If we win another great victory against them there, do you think we can bring this accursed war to an end?”
“We’ll be one step closer.
And the step we take this time will be bigger and deeper than any before it.”
“Deep enough to reach the Lord of Heaven?”
“I believe so.”
“Then the Kongtong Sect will stand with you.”
“We won’t stop until we reach the end.
If only for the sake of the souls who must now be under the care of the Primordial Heavenly Venerable, beyond those clouds.”
If Perfected Being Hyeoncheon had been giving off the same killing intent he’d shown while slaughtering the surviving Dark Heaven followers, I would have refused his offer.
But the old Daoist had lost so much, and his eyes were clear.
The same was true of the Kongtong Disciples, who had poured out their anger and grief.
“All right.”
And so Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and about a hundred Kongtong Disciples joined us.
But that was only the beginning.
“I, Hyuk Sopyung, a junior martial artist, humbly ask leave to answer for my sect’s sins.”
Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.
Along with him, more than three hundred Zhongnan Sect Disciples who had barely survived the bloody battle set down their weapons and knelt.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom.
The two elders of their sect were dead, and now the Disciples knew what they had done.
Shame and grief filled their faces.
Blood trickled between their tightly clenched teeth.
If the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, the Zhongnan Sect Leader, hadn’t been unconscious from his severe injuries, he would have knelt beside them and asked to answer for those sins too.
Perfected Being Hyeoncheon watched the Zhongnan Disciples in silence for a long while.
Then he spoke.
“A father’s sins do not belong to his children, nor a master’s to his Disciples.
Why, then, do the Disciples of Zhongnan ask me to hold them to account?”
“Still, if you insist on accepting a penalty, so be it.
Follow Daoist Friend Jin here and walk a straight, honorable path.
Let that be the Zhongnan Sect’s new way.”
At the old Daoist’s wise and compassionate words, Hyuk Sopyung and the Zhongnan Disciples bowed deeply.
Then they gave me a fist-and-palm salute with the utmost respect.
“We wish to walk the righteous path without straying an inch.
Great Hero Jin, we ask to join you.”
It was the first time I’d come face-to-face with Hyuk Sopyung since the incident at the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
He had once been the Zhongnan Sect’s most promising young prodigy, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
The gap between us had grown even wider than before.
Even after spending several days alongside the Zhongnan Sect in Gansu, I’d only ever passed him at a distance.
Maybe that was why I’d only just noticed how much more serious his bearing had become, how much deeper his gaze.
“I’d be glad to have you.”
For once, I accepted an offer with proper courtesy.
Our numbers had swelled to around five hundred with the two sects joining us, and someone watching it all came over.

Don’t you think?”
“Maybe.
Still better than padding our numbers with any old riffraff.”
“Funny.
My ears are itching.
Must be my imagination.”
“Maybe not.”
The new Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate gave a dry laugh at my feigned innocence, then pointed to his new followers, lined up in orderly ranks.
“Five hundred.
Time was short, but I chose them carefully from the volunteers.
They may not measure up to the Disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang, but I can vouch for their loyalty and fighting spirit.”
“So you’re putting them under my command?”
“No.
I’d be grateful if you let them come with you.”
“What?”
“I, Sama Pyo, Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, and five hundred men ask to join the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master.
Please allow us to fight for the realm and make up, however little, for our past wrongs.”
For a moment, I couldn’t speak.
I might not have been able to hold back the emotion welling up inside me if a giant with a little old man dangling from his neck hadn’t shouted right then.
“Taishan’s going!
Taishan’s going too!
Taishan will go with the Pavilion Master to the end!”
“Goddamn it!
Stop bouncing around so much!
Please!”
Everyone burst out laughing at once, as if they’d planned it.
Me, Sama Pyo, the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, and the survivors of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Even Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, whose expression never changed whether he was happy or sad.
“You martial artists are quite an amusing lot.”
“Really?
Since you brought it up, want to hear something even funnier?”
“Something funnier?”
“Yeah.
It’s about a certain Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who kept talking back to a Marquis like he was his equal and is now on the verge of being forcibly discharged.
The funny thing is, he has the same surname as you.
What a coincidence, huh?”
“...Is that how you’re going to play this?”
“Then do your best.
So I don’t have to.”
Jeong Hogun shook his head as though there was no winning with me.
Then he stood as straight as an iron tower and saluted.
“Then please give your orders.”
“Qinghai.
We’re going to Qinghai Province.
At full speed.”
“I, Jeong Hogun, Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, accept the solemn order of the Most Honorable Marquis of Shangshan.”
And so, two days ago, the Embroidered Uniform Guard joined us as the final piece of our force.
Now nearly two thousand strong, we took a brief rest and headed straight for Qinghai Province.
A few people raised the cautious possibility that Dark Heaven might target Gansu again.
The Bow Saint put those concerns to rest with a single remark.
“The North is moving.”
Naturally, she didn’t mean northern Gansu.
She meant the North of the entire world, divided by the Great Wall—and the two powers that ruled that vast land.
The fierce tiger of Hebei: the Hebei Peng Family.
And the Azure Dragon of Shanxi Province: the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who had now claimed even the skies above the green grasslands.
“Arrows may fly at different speeds, but so long as they hold their course, each will eventually strike its target.”
The Bow Saint and the Embroidered Uniform Guard, for example, were arrows shot ahead of the rest.
It was a metaphor worthy of the Bow Saint.
No one argued after that.
Not merely because she was the Bow Saint.
Everyone knew that with the Azure Dragon and the fierce tiger of the North spreading their wings and baring their claws, Gansu was reasonably safe.
And the brief purge just before we left Gansu was enough to wipe out any possible future threat.

I’ll hear your last words.”

There must have been some misunderstanding!”

Wide eyes.
Trembling lips.

How much more shocked must those men have been, after knowing him for decades?
Sama Pyo went on.
There was a trace of bitterness toward his father in his voice, and he looked at the men as though they were insects.
“So.
Any last words?”
That did it.
“You—you little brat, with the blood barely dry on your head!
You dare kill me, your uncle in all but name?!”
“Heh.
Heh heh.
So this is how it ends.”
A cornered rat had only two choices.

chapters.title: Chapter 1066
paragraphs: Ding!
System Entered Qinghai Province.
The System notification chimed just as I was striding toward Great Sir with my fist clenched. I stopped.
“You made the right call. There’s nothing to gain by hitting someone who’s already in rough shape... Are you listening to me?”
“Shh.”
Hyuk Mujin had sighed in relief, apparently thinking I’d changed my mind. I signaled for him to be quiet and looked around.
Dense forest lay under the cover of darkness, and insects chirped here and there.
Nothing about the landscape had changed, but all of us had just crossed an invisible boundary. The System was always accurate. It never lied.
Great Sir had somehow fulfilled the task he’d been given. Now he looked as puzzled as the question marks that had floated above his head.
“What’s wrong, Jang Sam?”
“...I’m Jin Taekyung, not Jang Sam.”
To be honest, I’d doubted him right up to the end.

Following someone who couldn’t even remember his own name was hardly a wise decision. He’d kept changing direction along the way, too. Even Sama Pyo, who’d spent his whole life in Gansu Province, had questioned him more than once.
Still.
It worked out.
We’d shaved at least two days off the journey I’d expected. The mountain route had been rough, but the time we’d saved gave us a chance to rest and build up our Stamina.
The question is, how does this guy know a route like this?
The obvious question came back to me. But then Great Sir opened his mouth in a jaw-splitting yawn, and I found myself shaking my head.
What good would it do to keep wondering? The man had been all over the place for ages, and the System had stamped him with its official Madman seal. There was no room left for doubt.
What mattered was that Great Sir was at least on our side. Thanks to him, we had reached Qinghai Province.
More precisely, the area near Qinghai Province’s northwest border.
And this place is...
Right.
Enemy territory, now under Dark Heaven’s control and filled with countless dangers.
Some three thousand people.

That was no small number. In the modern world, a Guild with that many Hunters would easily count as a major one. Even a sect among the Nine Sects and One Gang—apart from the Beggars’ Sect—would have to gather its lay Disciples from outside its main stronghold to reach that number.
But everything was relative.
Dark Heaven’s army invading Qinghai rivaled the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples of old. Against it, three thousand people were no more than fireflies before the sun.
This is urgent, but if we rush straight in with everyone this exhausted, we’ll be the ones getting slaughtered.
So I proposed a day’s rest in the mountains where we’d stopped. No one objected.
Not even Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, whom I’d expected to be the hardest to persuade. If anything, he went out of his way to show me more respect than necessary, which only left me flustered.
“A sound judgment indeed. Very well. What are your orders after we rest?”
“Sorry? My orders?”
“Is something wrong? If you’d rather call them commands, I don’t mind.”
“...I’d rather you curse me out. Why are you doing this to me?”
Was this how a family heir felt when his grandfather’s generation bowed deeply to him during a holiday gathering?
At my thoroughly disconcerted reaction, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon gave a quiet laugh and said something I hadn’t expected.
“Perhaps you should look around you once in a while.”
“What do you mean...?”
“See how many people stand around you. See how they look at you. That will tell you where you stand now.”
Only then did I notice how many eyes were fixed on me.
The admiration and goodwill in their gazes were so clear I felt I could reach out and touch them. Gratitude showed in their faint smiles, impossible to hide.
Then Perfected Being Hyeoncheon’s warm voice drifted into my ears.
“Whether you ask, instruct, or command us makes no difference. We all owe you a great debt.”
“A debt...”
“In Murim, gratitude and grudges must be repaid. But I have forgiven my grudge. Now I wish to repay the kindness shown to me. I expect they feel the same.”
I thought for a moment about how they must feel.

They’d lost comrades they’d shared years of hardship with, family, Senior and Junior Brothers. Before they’d even begun to recover from the fear and sorrow they’d felt on the battlefield, they’d chosen of their own accord to follow me into another deadly place.
They had come to repay a debt, but they were also driven by a desire for revenge that would bring darkness to this land.
And that desire was itself a light against the darkness.
“Ah.”
It was a strange feeling. One I couldn’t imagine ever getting used to.
I had no idea what to say.
But the old Daoist, whose wisdom matched his long life, didn’t demand a reply.
Pat, pat.
He gave my shoulder a couple of silent pats and walked away. Everyone else’s attention remained on me.
The Disciples of the Kongtong and Zhongnan Sects.
The martial artists of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the Black Dragon Demon Gate.
Even Jeok Cheongang and Bow Saint, standing among the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, merely nodded in silence.
As though they’d follow me to the end, even if I were headed straight for hell.
With some three thousand people watching me, I slowly opened my mouth.
And at the very moment the suffocating silence broke, a thought suddenly struck me.
How can it be this quiet?
Only then did I realize that the loud chirping of insects hidden throughout the thick forest had stopped at some point.
The birds perched high in the branches had vanished, too.
A chill ran down my spine.
Rumble. Rumble.
A faint tremor finally reached us from far away. With it came the eerie cry of something unknown, carried to my ears on the desolate wind.
Grrrk.
“...Shit.”
The curse slipped out on reflex.
I tightened my grip on White Flame’s shaft and stared past the darkness at the enemies coming to meet their unexpected visitors.
Then I gave my first command in Qinghai Province.
“Prepare for battle.”
Shing! Shing! Shing!
Countless waves of steel rose all at once, their cold gleam lighting up the darkness—and revealing the enemies who had approached behind its veil.
At the low groan that escaped someone’s lips, the enemy crawling up the ridge ahead of the others tilted his head.
Plop. Plop.
Pale brain matter dripped from his skull. Nearly half his head was already gone.
Since a time so distant it had left no written record, people had called a vast mountain range at the far western edge of the world:
“The land closest to heaven, its highest peaks touching the clouds...”
The Blood Lord murmured the words to himself, looked around, and nodded.
The mountain range stretched on in endless, overlapping ridges, its many peaks rising here and there. It was majestic and beautiful enough to make anyone gasp.
“Quite a sight. I can see why people of the Central Plains hold this place sacred. And why those worthless Kunlun Sect Daoists fought so desperately to protect it. Don’t you agree?”
At the Blood Lord’s sudden question, the Grand Sorceress, seated on a large rock and making strange gestures with her hands, answered,
“You seem rather taken with the scenery.”
“Well, Tianshan is bleak. You can’t deny that.”
“Then why not formally ask to join the Kunlun Sect? Who knows? Perhaps you’ll become its Sect Leader someday.”
The mockery was obvious, but the Blood Lord didn’t react as she’d intended. He stared at her with an odd look, then shrugged.
“Not a tempting offer. Got anything better?”
His easy reply made the Grand Sorceress frown.
“What’s gotten into you?”
“What do you mean?”
“You weren’t like this before.”
“Wasn’t I?”
The glib answer was nothing like the man she remembered. As she watched him, irritation welled up inside her.
Deranged monster. Acting as if he hasn’t a care in the world.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had been a bloodthirsty killer, but she found the Blood Lord even harder to stomach.
Stupid, vicious, and utterly shameless.
Those three qualities gave her ample reason to dislike him. But something else bothered her more.
Why does that person keep someone like him so close?
She couldn’t understand it.
As far as she had seen, the Blood Lord was neither more skilled in martial arts nor more cunning than the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress who had died before him.

But there was no denying that, unlike the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, a mere piece on the board, the Blood Lord had his master’s trust. And the fact that he stood on equal footing with her only made her more uncomfortable.
And then there was the person sitting just a few jang away, giving off a dreadful stench the entire time.
Jingle. Jangle.
The Grand Sorceress grimaced at the man in black. He sat cross-legged, muttering without pause.

The foul odor drifting over on the wind was bad enough, but the dull, grating jingling of his bells every time he moved was even worse. The more she heard it, the more it grated on her, as though an awl were digging into her ears and unsettling her mind.
“Who is he?”
“My subordinate,” the Blood Lord answered readily.
“You had someone like him working for you? There’s something oddly familiar about him. And unpleasant.”
“That would be because he’s a sorcerer.”
“What?”
“Oh, don’t get the wrong idea. He’s a different kind of sorcerer from a certain sharp-tongued bitch. He only joined my ranks recently, actually.”
The Grand Sorceress’s eyes widened as she caught his meaning.
“Then...”
“That’s right. Until a few months ago, he served another Demon Lord. Though, to be precise...”
The Blood Lord’s mouth curved into a smile.
“I suppose he was that Demon Lord’s Disciple, rather than his subordinate.”
At that very moment—
Clatter.
The bell rang again, louder and deeper than before, and the man in black raised his head.
Pale skin. Eyes with a bluish cast.
And a dry voice, without a hint of emotion.
“I found it.”
Not so long ago, Ma Sanbao had held the imperial court in his grasp as the East Depot’s Brush-Holding Eunuch. At his report, the Blood Lord smiled with satisfaction.
“Now that is very welcome news.”

We’d shaved at least two days off the journey I’d expected.
The mountain route had been rough, but the time we’d saved gave us a chance to rest and build up our Stamina.
The question is, how does this guy know a route like this?
The obvious question came back to me.
But then Great Sir opened his mouth in a jaw-splitting yawn, and I found myself shaking my head.
What good would it do to keep wondering?
The man had been all over the place for ages, and the System had stamped him with its official Madman seal.
There was no room left for doubt.
What mattered was that Great Sir was at least on our side.
Thanks to him, we had reached Qinghai Province.
More precisely, the area near Qinghai Province’s northwest border.
And this place is...
Right.
Enemy territory, now under Dark Heaven’s control and filled with countless dangers.
Some three thousand people.
That was no small number.
In the modern world, a Guild with that many Hunters would easily count as a major one.
Even a sect among the Nine Sects and One Gang—apart from the Beggars’ Sect—would have to gather its lay Disciples from outside its main stronghold to reach that number.
But everything was relative.
Dark Heaven’s army invading Qinghai rivaled the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples of old.
Against it, three thousand people were no more than fireflies before the sun.
This is urgent, but if we rush straight in with everyone this exhausted, we’ll be the ones getting slaughtered.
So I proposed a day’s rest in the mountains where we’d stopped.
No one objected.
Not even Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, whom I’d expected to be the hardest to persuade.
If anything, he went out of his way to show me more respect than necessary, which only left me flustered.
“A sound judgment indeed.
Very well.
What are your orders after we rest?”
“Sorry?
My orders?”
“Is something wrong?
If you’d rather call them commands, I don’t mind.”
“...I’d rather you curse me out.
Why are you doing this to me?”
Was this how a family heir felt when his grandfather’s generation bowed deeply to him during a holiday gathering?
At my thoroughly disconcerted reaction, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon gave a quiet laugh and said something I hadn’t expected.
“Perhaps you should look around you once in a while.”
“What do you mean...?”
“See how many people stand around you.
See how they look at you.
That will tell you where you stand now.”
Only then did I notice how many eyes were fixed on me.
The admiration and goodwill in their gazes were so clear I felt I could reach out and touch them.
Gratitude showed in their faint smiles, impossible to hide.
Then Perfected Being Hyeoncheon’s warm voice drifted into my ears.
“Whether you ask, instruct, or command us makes no difference.
We all owe you a great debt.”
“A debt...”
“In Murim, gratitude and grudges must be repaid.
But I have forgiven my grudge.
Now I wish to repay the kindness shown to me.
I expect they feel the same.”
I thought for a moment about how they must feel.
They’d lost comrades they’d shared years of hardship with, family, Senior and Junior Brothers.
Before they’d even begun to recover from the fear and sorrow they’d felt on the battlefield, they’d chosen of their own accord to follow me into another deadly place.
They had come to repay a debt, but they were also driven by a desire for revenge that would bring darkness to this land.
And that desire was itself a light against the darkness.
“Ah.”
It was a strange feeling.
One I couldn’t imagine ever getting used to.
I had no idea what to say.
But the old Daoist, whose wisdom matched his long life, didn’t demand a reply.
Pat, pat.
He gave my shoulder a couple of silent pats and walked away.
Everyone else’s attention remained on me.
The Disciples of the Kongtong and Zhongnan Sects.
The martial artists of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the Black Dragon Demon Gate.
Even Jeok Cheongang and Bow Saint, standing among the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, merely nodded in silence.
As though they’d follow me to the end, even if I were headed straight for hell.
With some three thousand people watching me, I slowly opened my mouth.
And at the very moment the suffocating silence broke, a thought suddenly struck me.
How can it be this quiet?
Only then did I realize that the loud chirping of insects hidden throughout the thick forest had stopped at some point.
The birds perched high in the branches had vanished, too.
A chill ran down my spine.
Rumble.
Rumble.
A faint tremor finally reached us from far away.
With it came the eerie cry of something unknown, carried to my ears on the desolate wind.
Grrrk.
“...Shit.”
The curse slipped out on reflex.
I tightened my grip on White Flame’s shaft and stared past the darkness at the enemies coming to meet their unexpected visitors.
Then I gave my first command in Qinghai Province.
“Prepare for battle.”
Shing!
Shing!
Shing!
Countless waves of steel rose all at once, their cold gleam lighting up the darkness—and revealing the enemies who had approached behind its veil.
At the low groan that escaped someone’s lips, the enemy crawling up the ridge ahead of the others tilted his head.
Plop.
Plop.
Pale brain matter dripped from his skull.
Nearly half his head was already gone.
Since a time so distant it had left no written record, people had called a vast mountain range at the far western edge of the world:
“The land closest to heaven, its highest peaks touching the clouds...”
The Blood Lord murmured the words to himself, looked around, and nodded.
The mountain range stretched on in endless, overlapping ridges, its many peaks rising here and there.
It was majestic and beautiful enough to make anyone gasp.
“Quite a sight.
I can see why people of the Central Plains hold this place sacred.
And why those worthless Kunlun Sect Daoists fought so desperately to protect it.
Don’t you agree?”
At the Blood Lord’s sudden question, the Grand Sorceress, seated on a large rock and making strange gestures with her hands, answered,
“You seem rather taken with the scenery.”
“Well, Tianshan is bleak.
You can’t deny that.”
“Then why not formally ask to join the Kunlun Sect?
Who knows?
Perhaps you’ll become its Sect Leader someday.”
The mockery was obvious, but the Blood Lord didn’t react as she’d intended.
He stared at her with an odd look, then shrugged.
“Not a tempting offer.
Got anything better?”
His easy reply made the Grand Sorceress frown.
“What’s gotten into you?”
“What do you mean?”
“You weren’t like this before.”
“Wasn’t I?”
The glib answer was nothing like the man she remembered.
As she watched him, irritation welled up inside her.
Deranged monster.
Acting as if he hasn’t a care in the world.
The Blood-Sword Demon Lord had been a bloodthirsty killer, but she found the Blood Lord even harder to stomach.
Stupid, vicious, and utterly shameless.
Those three qualities gave her ample reason to dislike him.
But something else bothered her more.
Why does that person keep someone like him so close?
She couldn’t understand it.
As far as she had seen, the Blood Lord was neither more skilled in martial arts nor more cunning than the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress who had died before him.
But there was no denying that, unlike the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, a mere piece on the board, the Blood Lord had his master’s trust.
And the fact that he stood on equal footing with her only made her more uncomfortable.
And then there was the person sitting just a few jang away, giving off a dreadful stench the entire time.
Jingle.
Jangle.
The Grand Sorceress grimaced at the man in black.
He sat cross-legged, muttering without pause.
The foul odor drifting over on the wind was bad enough, but the dull, grating jingling of his bells every time he moved was even worse.
The more she heard it, the more it grated on her, as though an awl were digging into her ears and unsettling her mind.
“Who is he?”
“My subordinate,” the Blood Lord answered readily.
“You had someone like him working for you?
There’s something oddly familiar about him.
And unpleasant.”
“That would be because he’s a sorcerer.”
“What?”
“Oh, don’t get the wrong idea.
He’s a different kind of sorcerer from a certain sharp-tongued bitch.
He only joined my ranks recently, actually.”
The Grand Sorceress’s eyes widened as she caught his meaning.
“Then...”
“That’s right.
Until a few months ago, he served another Demon Lord.
Though, to be precise...”
The Blood Lord’s mouth curved into a smile.
“I suppose he was that Demon Lord’s Disciple, rather than his subordinate.”
At that very moment—
Clatter.
The bell rang again, louder and deeper than before, and the man in black raised his head.
Pale skin.
Eyes with a bluish cast.
And a dry voice, without a hint of emotion.
“I found it.”
Not so long ago, Ma Sanbao had held the imperial court in his grasp as the East Depot’s Brush-Holding Eunuch.
At his report, the Blood Lord smiled with satisfaction.
“Now that is very welcome news.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1067
paragraphs: Half a shichen.
That was how long Qinghai’s first battle had lasted, from beginning to end.
“So this is where you were.”
The forest was thick with the smell of blood. I sat on the body of an enemy I didn’t recognize, catching my breath, and turned toward the voice.
Squish.
Footsteps strode through blood and mud. A familiar face came into view, clad in armor stained red, its original golden luster gone.
“Shouldn’t that be, ‘So this is where you were, sir’?”
Jeong Hogun, a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, let out a small sigh.
“So this is where you were, sir. Happy now?”
“Not even close. You dropped the ‘sir’ again in your very next sentence.”
“...Give it a rest. We’ve both had a hard time.”
“I was about to. How bad are our losses?”
“Hardly worth calling them losses. Around thirty casualties, and not a single death.”
Jeong Hogun glanced at the heaps of bodies around us and added, “Considering we wiped out more than a thousand enemies, it’s a miracle.”
Three thousand against one thousand.
We’d had the advantage in numbers from the start, but winning without a single death was an absurdly decisive victory. All the more so when it had taken only half a shichen.
Still, my answer was matter-of-fact.
“It wasn’t a miracle. It was only natural.”
“I can’t argue with that. The difference in strength was overwhelming.”
Our troops were all handpicked elites, which had helped. But the Supreme Peak masters had made a far greater difference.
Bow Saint. Jeok Cheongang. Perfected Being Hyeoncheon. Me.
And, last of all, the Great Sir—though he hadn’t been much help.
With forces like that, losing would have been harder than winning.
There was only one problem...
“How’s everyone doing?”
“What do they look like?”
Jeong Hogun’s immediate question made me click my tongue.
Honestly, I didn’t need to ask. Everywhere I looked, faces were stiff. Despite the overwhelming victory and the few injuries we’d suffered, our allies were pale, with faint fear in their eyes.
As though they’d seen something terrible they were never meant to see.
Which they had.
The unknown enemy still writhing beneath my ass was a monster by any definition.
Grrk. Grrrk.
A faint, guttural cry leaked from its split throat.
Only then did Jeong Hogun notice it. His brow furrowed.
“It’s still alive?”
“Maybe. If you can call this alive.”
I gazed down at the cursed monster.

Its limbs had been horribly severed, and its body was rotting. It had clearly died days ago, yet it had never crossed the Sanzu River. It remained in this world, struggling stubbornly, unable even to remember who it had been in life.
But the two characters stitched into its torn, ragged clothes still remembered their owner.
“Kunlun...”
I nodded quietly at Jeong Hogun’s low murmur.
That was right.
This monster was a Disciple of the Kunlun Sect.
No—it had been one.
“I heard there were casualties during the retreat from Kunlun Mountain. I suppose this was one of them.”
“Probably.”
“Did you know him?”
I shook my head at Jeong Hogun’s cautious question.
“No. Not at all.”

I’d met Hak Woo—the Kunlun Cloud Dragon, the Kunlun Sect’s greatest young prodigy and a member of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—at the Star-Array Grand Banquet. But I didn’t recognize the face of this Daoist who’d become a monster.
Still, I had a rough idea who might have made him this way.
“Looks familiar, doesn’t it?”
“Yes.”
Jeong Hogun’s eyes darkened.
“Cang Gong. It’s astonishingly similar to the dark arts he used.”
Wei Zhong.
The East Depot’s Seal-Holding Eunuch, known as Cang Gong, had harbored two deep secrets.
First, he was the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, one of the Lord of Heaven’s loyal servants.
Second, he was a descendant of the Maoshan Sect, which the imperial family had wiped out long ago.
But even after Wei Zhong met his end at my hands, the Maoshan Sect’s line hadn’t died out.
“Ma Sanbao. It has to be him.”
The Disciple who’d inherited everything from Wei Zhong.
Like his Master, he’d worn a mask while operating in secret as an East Depot eunuch. We’d never found his body. That could mean only one thing.
“I wondered where he’d gone. Looks like he survived and joined Dark Heaven after all.”
Of course, it might not be Ma Sanbao.
According to Jeok Cheongang, the Corpse Art Wei Zhong had demonstrated had gone far beyond its old limits. That meant it had been improved with the Lord of Heaven’s help.
But even if Dark Heaven had trained others in the Corpse Art, none of them would have reached the level of Ma Sanbao, who’d learned directly from Wei Zhong.
Besides...
Qinghai is an important battlefield for them and for us. They’ll be throwing more into this fight than ever.
Dark Heaven’s army of a hundred thousand had already swallowed half of Qinghai Province.

I had no idea why the Lord of Heaven had intended to lose in Gansu, but this time he was sure to commit everything he had. Even Dark Heaven, with strength far beyond the Demonic Cult of old, wouldn’t simply throw away a hundred thousand troops as fodder.
Ma Sanbao is one of the pieces they need to win. They won’t leave him out.
A thought flashed through my mind, and I swallowed a groan.
If all hundred thousand enemies had been turned into jiangshi, the disaster would be impossible to stop.
And worse...
The Lord of Heaven might appear on the battlefield himself.
I’d never even faced him properly, yet the thought of those two words made my heart sink.
How could I forget?
The Lord of Heaven had appeared only once, and I remembered every moment of it clearly.
Interesting. Very interesting.
The one who’d smiled at Jeok Cheongang and me that day hadn’t been the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
It had been a demon borrowing a human body. The darkness of the abyss itself. An absolute being whom no one seemed capable of opposing.
Until next time.
But after that day, the Lord of Heaven never appeared before me again.
He stayed crouched in the darkness, watching everything.
Even as his loyal servants, including the Western Heaven Demon Lord, met their ends one by one. Even as the plans he’d spent years and considerable effort preparing were dismantled piece by piece.
He never appeared.
But he watched it all, waiting for a moment no one in the world could foresee. A moment only he knew.
And deep down, I sensed that the moment he wanted wasn’t far off. I sensed, too, that it was deeply and unmistakably connected to me.
What is he trying to get through me?
Just as I turned that unanswerable question over in my head—
Whoosh! Thwack!
A sharp whistle cut through the air. Snapping out of my thoughts, I heard a shout from not far away.
“Oh, I got it! I got it!”
“Wow! Sir! Amazing! Taishan is truly impressed!”
“Ahem. Did you see that? When I put my mind to it, something like this is easy.”
I looked over to find the Great Sir holding a bird and looking rather pleased with himself.
Its head was smashed to a pulp. It looked like it had died from being hit by a stone.
Taishan was staring at the Great Sir—or, more precisely, at the bird—and drooling.
“Tasty—no, impressive! Taishan will start a fire, so let’s hurry and roast it!”
A campfire in the middle of enemy territory. It was the kind of bullshit that made everyone else furious, me included. But one lunatic felt differently.
“Young friend, you know how to show proper courtesy. For your trouble, I’ll give you some of my meat. Which part would you like?”
“The legs! Definitely the legs!”
“You’ve eaten your share of chicken, I see. Fine, I’ll give you one.”
“Both! All of them!”
“...Don’t push your luck.”
The Great Sir suddenly sobered up. Taishan drooped his head in disappointment, and that was when Namho, perched on Taishan’s shoulder as comfortably as though it were his usual seat, spoke up.
“You’re all making damn fools of yourselves. That thing stinks like hell, wherever it came from. Eat it? Bullshit.”
His words brought a thought to mind.
Wait. Could it be?
The moment Jeong Hogun examined the bird, my suspicion became certainty.
“It’s rotting. The bones are showing.”
“Which means...”
“Looks like the monsters aren’t only on the ground.”
It had been strange enough for a bird to remain there after strangers invaded its territory.
As everyone caught on and turned to look at him, the Great Sir blinked in confusion.
“Is something wrong? It was staring right at me from a branch, so...”
“It was staring at you?”
He nodded.
“I’m certain. Its eyes were bloodred, too. It made me so uneasy that I threw a stone at it.”
“...A Familiar?”
“Hm? What was that?”
“Nothing. Just talking to myself.”
I waved a hand at the Great Sir and stared silently into the air.
Dawn was only now spreading from the east. In its light, I could make out shapes here and there among the branches high overhead.
Monsters hidden in the darkness, brought back to life by its power.
They were already watching us.
My thoughts turned cold as I slowly rose. Then I spoke to the Great Sir, who still looked confused.
“If you see any more birds like that, kill every one of them.”
“Every one?”
“Yes. Every one.”
“That seems a bit much. Aren’t they precious lives, too?”
I considered my answer for a moment.
“They’re harmful birds.”
“Oh. Then I’ll kill them.”
“Please.”
I patted his shoulder and started to leave, but stopped when I remembered something I’d forgotten.
I reached out and murmured, “Infinite Life Buddha.”
Stab.
The monster stopped moving completely. I left it—the Kunlun Sect Disciple—behind and walked away.
There was no time to spare now.
Eyes were already watching us, and pursuers would soon be on our heels.
