I simply went where my feet took me, where the wind blew.
The deaths of strangers I’d never met didn’t trouble me much.
People saw Jeok Cheongang as the foremost of the Ten Kings, one of the great figures of the orthodox faction.
But the truth was different.
He was a free man.
Like the Sect Leaders of the Fire Gate Clan before him, he belonged to none of the orthodox, unorthodox, or demonic factions.
He had walked only his own path.
—Perhaps that’s why the title of Great Hero, which stuck to me before I knew it, always felt like clothes that didn’t fit.
—But you deserve to be called one.
—No.
That’s wrong.
Jeok Cheongang answered firmly and fixed me with a deep, searching gaze.
—Only someone who fears the pain of others and knows how to shed tears deserves to be called a Great Hero.
Someone like you.
—But remember one thing.
If you don’t want to shed tears later, you must first overcome the fear in front of you.
Then Jeok Cheongang added quietly,
—Only then do you become a hero.
A hero.
A hero, huh.
I mouthed those two words in my mind.
They had always felt so far away.
Then I gave a bitter smile.
—I never wanted to be one.
—That doesn’t matter.
Wanting to be a hero isn’t what makes you one.
You earn the title when the world calls you one.
—Like how they call you a Great Hero, Old Master?
—What?
—You just said it yourself.
You never went out of your way to pursue a grand cause.
You went where your feet took you, where the wind blew—and before you knew it, people were calling you a Great Hero.
Jeok Cheongang stared at me, eyes wide.
Then he licked his lips.
—You got me with that one.
—Let’s call it even.
—You haven’t lost your knack for running that mouth.
Now you’re finally starting to feel like the little hellion I knew.
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh and gestured with his chin beyond the wall.
—Well?
Still afraid?
—Yes.
I answered without hesitation, then added calmly,
—But I won’t look away from that fear.
Everyone carries fear somewhere in their heart.
But only those who admit it and face it head-on can find the strength to stand against it.
Just as I was doing now.
Rumble.
Rrrumble!
The rumbling grew stronger by the moment, and the ground shook as if an earthquake had struck.
I felt the powerful vibrations travel up the tall, sturdy wall and through my whole body.
At the same time, I saw him.
At the head of the enemy forces, so numerous I couldn’t begin to count them, one man was grinning as he looked straight at us.
The Blood Lord.
He looked quite different from the last time I’d seen him, but the moment I saw that crooked smile, I knew by instinct.
The thick killing intent and madness about him seemed as though they’d rub off if I touched him.
Even the Blood-Sword Demon Lord I’d defeated in Gansu couldn’t compare.
And in the instant we recognized each other, his lips moved.
“Looking up at you is a pain in the neck.
Why don’t you come down for a bit and say hello?”
His words rang out through the deafening rumble and clouds of dust.
Jeok Cheongang, who had already been staring hard at the Blood Lord, had a reddish gleam in his eyes.
“I was itching for a fight anyway.
How kind of him to offer.”
The Bow Saint immediately sensed what was coming and tried to stop him.
“He’s baiting you.
It couldn’t be more obvious.”
At her look for support, the Slaughter Saint, who had appeared out of nowhere and taken up a place on the wall, calmly nodded.
“Yeah, it’s crazy.”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow.
The Slaughter Saint added,
“Then again, no one here is in their right mind.”
As Jeok Cheongang’s brow smoothed, I delivered my solemn verdict.
“Let’s do it now.”
“Right.
It’s not like we’ll die or anything.”
Whoosh!
There wasn’t even time for anyone to stop us.
Reciting the number-one last words of men everywhere, the three of us sprang off the wall together.
Behind us came the sharpest, loudest shout I’d ever heard from the Bow Saint.
“I told you not to go!”
Uh.
Sorry.
The moment he saw three figures hurtling across the distant sky toward him, the Blood Lord muttered without realizing it,
“They’re crazy.
They’re actually coming?”
He’d only tossed out a casual remark.
After a few words between them, he hadn’t expected them to charge straight at him without a moment’s hesitation.
“What are they, half-mad fighting dogs...?”
The Blood Lord trailed off, more than a little taken aback.
By then, the three men had closed to a dozen or so zhang, moving like flashes of light.
They spoke at once.
“You told us to come down, you son of a bitch.”
“You’re lower than a dog.
You goddamned bastard.
Burning you alive wouldn’t be enough, you miserable—”
“So you’re the Blood Lord I’ve heard about.
I know this is a strange request for a first meeting, but would you mind calmly offering your neck and stepping aside?”
First came Jin Taekyung, whose curses had an oddly satisfying ring to them.
Then Jeok Cheongang, hurling every obscenity he knew.
And finally the Slaughter Saint, whom the Blood Lord was meeting for the first time.
For a moment, surprise had covered the Blood Lord’s anger.
Now he felt it surge back to the surface.
“Are you done talking?”
At the Blood Lord’s low voice, Jin Taekyung hesitated briefly and glanced at the Slaughter Saint.
“Anything else you’d like to say?”
“Probably not.
We’ve only just met, so I don’t have much to say.”
The Slaughter Saint had already been remarkably rude for someone meeting him for the first time, but Jin Taekyung merely nodded and answered the Blood Lord.
“This one says he’s done.”
Crack.
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth at that nonchalant response and opened his mouth.
Or tried to.
Before he could, another wave of obscenities swept over him.
“I’ll grind down every last bone in your body.
I’ll toss your flesh to the Nanman Beast Palace for feed, then scatter your remains in the Shaolin Temple latrines, and—”
“Ah, this one isn’t done yet.
Give him a moment.
Honestly, aren’t you a little curious what comes next?”
At that moment, the Blood Lord’s last thread of reason snapped.
His vision went white.
“Hah!”
KWA-A-A!
A powerful wave of qi swept out in every direction.
The immense internal energy packed into that single shout made Dark Heaven’s seemingly endless army and the people on the wall a hundred or so zhang away hold their breath.
But the three men closest to him, who felt the full force of it, were the exception.
Whoosh!
A single sharp gust cut through the billowing dust.
At its center, Jin Taekyung had already slashed down with his clear, almost transparent spearhead.
He grinned.
Just as the Blood Lord had before they came down from the wall.
“Why are you getting so worked up?
I’m just glad to see you after all this time.”
An explosion meant destruction.
Destruction, in turn, was bound up with Erasure.
The Blood Lord had gathered his anger and unleashed it all at once.
Now he stared at Jin Taekyung with eyes gone cold.
“You’re just the same as before.
That damned mouth of yours.”
The smile vanished from Jin Taekyung’s lips.
“This time will be different.
Everything else will be.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1092
paragraphs: To a martial artist, a wave of qi was power made manifest.
Jin Taekyung could feel that more clearly than ever now. He could feel just how terrifyingly powerful the enemy before him was.
Rumble.

The air refused to settle beneath the force of the Blood Lord’s qi. Faint tremors came from every direction, but Taekyung’s mind grew calm enough for him to answer evenly, despite the cold fire in the Blood Lord’s voice and gaze.
“You’re just the same as before. That damned mouth of yours.”
Taekyung let his smile fade. He raised his beloved spear, White Flame, and pointed it at the Blood Lord.
“This time will be different. Everything else will be.”
“Different? Ha!”
Now it was the Blood Lord’s turn to laugh. He eyed Taekyung with open contempt.

“I heard the Hidden Dragon had become a Divine Dragon, but you’re acting like you’ve gotten your hands on a dragon pearl, too. Struggle all you want. You’re still no match for me. You know that yourself, don’t you?”
To the Blood Lord’s surprise, Taekyung nodded readily.
“Yeah. Probably.”
“What?”
“Why the reaction? Shouldn’t you be a little happy I admitted it so honestly?”
The Blood Lord’s voice dropped, but Taekyung spoke before he could continue.
“I knew as soon as I saw you. I couldn’t tell exactly how strong you were.”
Even stones scattered along a roadside varied in size and shape. Why wouldn’t mountains tall enough to touch the clouds vary in height?
Taekyung had climbed from the very bottom of the Murim to the heights of Supreme Peak. The moment he came face-to-face with the Blood Lord, he understood.
“You’re stronger than me. No question.”
He didn’t know exactly how wide the gap was. But even if it was only one move—or half a move—Jin Taekyung accepted that the Blood Lord was the stronger one.

He remembered his not-so-distant past, when he’d been no better than an ant, helpless beneath a power so immense it felt absolute. Back then, the Blood Lord had seemed as unreachable as someone above the clouds.
“But you know what?”
Taekyung held the Blood Lord’s gaze as he asked the question quietly.
Past and present overlapped before his eyes. Alongside the knowledge that the Blood Lord was stronger came another realization, running down his spine like an electric current.
“Back then, I thought I could fight with everything I had and still never touch a hair on your head...”
His voice trailed off, and he smiled.
Only today had he understood. The Blood Lord whose mere presence had once left him struggling to breathe was no longer beyond the clouds.
“Now I feel like I could reach you just by stretching out my hand.”
The Blood Lord’s eyes widened. A dozen or so zhang away, Taekyung’s figure wavered like a mirage.
Fshh.
His shape remained, but his body was gone. There wasn’t even a trace of his presence, yet the killing intent within it was unmistakable.
Whooosh!
The Blood Lord heard the eerie sound clearly, as though the wind itself were howling.
At the same instant, he saw it.
Space warped under immense pressure. With Shifting Form and Position brought to its pinnacle, a spearhead outran sound and tore through the compressed air.
“Jin Taekyung!”
And then—
KWA-A-A!
The Blood Lord’s furious shout and the muffled boom of a sonic blast rang out as a blood-red flash clashed with a dark-blue wave, swallowing the world around them.
One exchange.
A single exchange was enough to show me the gap between the Blood Lord and me.
KRRRACK!
The Blood Lord swung his Red Blade like lightning, and it locked against White Flame’s spearhead. The resulting boom was nothing a pair of weapons should have been able to make.
Neither was the shock wave that followed.
Rumble!
The hard ground cracked like a spiderweb. My feet slid backward under the force, and everything in their path crumbled to dust.
“You dared wag that tongue at me when this is all you’ve got?”
Beyond our crossed weapons, his eyes flashed blood-red. His voice seethed with fury.
Killing intent I could almost touch. A terrifyingly vast surge of qi.
Strong.
I was surprised all over again. The Blood Lord had grown stronger, too, over the past year—long or short as that might seem.
At least half a move above me. No, a full move.
At Supreme Peak, a single move made an enormous difference.
But it wasn’t only his insight into the martial arts or the depth of his internal energy that surprised me.
Grnnnk.
My spearhead began to give way. Slowly—no, faster than that.
Beyond it was a red blade that flashed without any blood-red Force, and a muscular arm, bulging with veins as he squeezed out every ounce of strength.
That’s... not human strength.
I could tell by instinct. After spending years fighting monsters instead of humans, how could I not?
The physical power the Blood Lord was unleashing went far beyond human limits.
No. It was more than that.
One look at the skin exposed by the rips in his clothes told me enough to guess what he’d done over the past year.
“Unusual for a prosthetic arm.”
I put everything I had into holding back the force pressing against my spear and studied him. More precisely, I studied the arm swollen to an unnatural size and the marks that looked like seams.
The Blood Lord bared his teeth and growled at me.
“Everything is thanks to that person’s grace.”
The Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, had taken one of the Blood Lord’s arms during the Shaolin Bloodshed. The Blood Lord had fled.
He should have spent the rest of his life with one arm. Yet here he was with two, wielding this kind of strength. That could mean only one thing.
“Did you want to get stronger that badly? Enough to splice yourself together with a monster?”
“Then again, forget about me. If you wanted revenge on the Sword Saint, you’d have had to tear something off and stick it on. Right?”
Had I struck a nerve? Or had I figured out the truth too easily?
The Blood Lord glared at me, eyes wide, and clenched his teeth.
“I look forward to seeing whether you can still run that mouth after you’re dead.”
At that moment—
Crack—KWA-AANG!
His arm swelled larger still, as thick as an old tree trunk. With a force that could only have come from a monster, he knocked my spearhead upward.
Clang!
Even my Strength stat, which had been in triple digits for a long time, couldn’t withstand that combination of raw power and internal energy. The shaft flew into the air.
My grip tore open. In an instant, I was empty-handed, and the Blood Lord’s Red Blade traced a dazzling arc toward me.
Whoosh! KWAANG!
Crude and brutal, the strike could have smashed anything in its path. Another followed it, cutting through the air like lightning.
His blade pursued me as my feet kept moving, the blood-red Force at its edge bending like a whip.
Whish—slice!
Every hair on my body stood on end. The Force skimmed past, slicing off a few strands of hair before slamming into the ground.
KWAANG! Rrrumble!
The earth shook like an earthquake, unable to withstand the tremendous force carried by the Force.
Dust billowed across dozens of zhang in every direction, but even that couldn’t block the Blood Lord’s view.
“This! This is all you’ve got!”
Whoosh!
The dust cloud split beneath a fierce sonic boom. I threw myself to the side on instinct, dodging the blood-red Force plunging down like an axe swung by some ancient giant.
Slice!
The ground split in two and opened a pitch-black maw.
I’d gotten out of the way in time, but the wind from the strike alone left me covered in blood. The Blood Lord smirked.
“Narye tagon. I heard you’d become the Divine Dragon while I was away, so I expected more. Instead, I find a lazy donkey rolling around on the ground.”
To martial artists—especially proud masters—Narye tagon was humiliation itself. Nobody who was anybody in the Murim wanted to be seen rolling through the dirt.
I didn’t care.

In low-level dungeons, I’d flattened myself against damp cave floors to avoid poison darts fired by kobolds. When an enemy got too close for my spear, I’d gone for the eyes or head-butted them without hesitation.
A character in a pirate manga that still hasn’t ended once said a wound on the back was a swordsman’s shame. I’ve never agreed with that.
“A wound on your back just fucking hurts. You have to be alive to feel ashamed.”
“What?”
I stopped moving.
The Blood Lord’s face seemed to ask what the hell I was going on about. I stood up, my body aching, and continued.
“I know it’s nonsense, so stop staring at me like that. You’re so cute I want to bite you to death.”
“You little—!”
“And what the fuck does it matter whether I’m a dragon or a donkey? You’re the one who tore the limbs off some monster nobody’s ever heard of and stuck them onto yourself.”
A heavy Patriot missile of a fact was what hurt the most.
Grind.
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth so hard they seemed ready to break and started forward again.
Or tried to.
The killing intent around him thickened. Blood-red Force stirred around his blade. Then a tremendous explosion jolted his long-paralyzed reason back to life.
KWA-AANG!
The boom shook everything around us. It had come from behind him.
The Blood Lord had chased me for over a hundred zhang, raining attacks down on me. The two giants who’d filled the opening he left behind were none other than the Fire King and the Slaughter Saint.
Crack—boom!
Flames erupted everywhere, and fountains of blood sprayed without pause.
Only then did the Blood Lord realize what was happening. He shot me a blood-red glare, but I just shrugged.
“Baiting you. Obvious as can be.”
“You—!”
“Oh, I can’t take all the credit. Someone said something pretty similar a little while ago.”
At that moment—
Whoooosh!
From the city wall, now much closer, a streak of light like a bolt of lightning pierced the pale dust cloud and plunged down.
KWA-A-AANG!

chapters.title: Chapter 1093
paragraphs: KWA-A-A-ANG!
The deafening boom left Jeok Cheongang’s ears ringing. Then a tremor ran through the ground. He turned to look behind him and finally let out a sigh of relief.
The old hag’s joined the fight.
Flashes of light were still streaking through the cloud of dust.
Once he saw that the Bow Saint was helping Jin Taekyung, part of him could finally relax. With her there, his Disciple would be safe.
At least for the brief time Jeok Cheongang needed to accomplish his goal.
I was worried sick... Maybe I didn’t need to be.

In Jeok Cheongang’s judgment, Jin Taekyung still wasn’t a match for the Blood Lord. That was why he hadn’t been able to hide his unease, even after hearing the Sound Transmission that had reached his ear moments ago.
“I’ll draw out the Blood Lord and buy us time. You two should target their main force.”
“What?”
“Don’t worry. You know my life motto, right?”
Of course he did.
However thick or thin his life might be, Taekyung meant to survive and make it last.
But if everything in the world went according to one’s wishes, every martial artist in the land would be a Supreme Peak master, and the common people would live long, healthy lives.
So Jeok Cheongang had firmly opposed the idea.
No—he’d meant to oppose it.
Before he could respond to that carefree answer, Jin Taekyung had charged out without hesitation to face the Blood Lord.
You idiot. Don’t you know your life is worth protecting?

Yet despite the thought, a smile had found its way onto Jeok Cheongang’s lips. It was plain enough that the Slaughter Saint, who was stirring up a bloodstorm not far away, couldn’t hold back a comment.
“I know you adore your one and only Disciple, but are you really so eager to die that you—”
He stopped mid-sentence and caught his breath, twisting aside.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Three streaks of sword light carved through the air, missing him by inches. At the same time, a flash glinted from the Slaughter Saint’s sleeve as he spun in midair.
KLANG! Thud!
Two sparks—and the sickening sound of a blade piercing flesh.
Three black-robed men clad head to toe in pitch-black armor had charged at him like bolts of lightning. They faltered and stepped back.
Or rather, two of them did.
Thump.
The third fell like a rotting tree. A dagger the Slaughter Saint had just thrown was buried deep between the eyeholes of his helmet, which sat so low that his face was completely hidden.
“One down.”
The Slaughter Saint landed smoothly, as if nothing had happened. Jeok Cheongang, who had just swept away dozens of enemies with a flaming punch, shook his head.
“I don’t think so.”
“...What do you mean?”
“What do you think?”
Jeok Cheongang jerked his chin toward the fallen man.
“That.”
At that very moment—
Thrust.
The man they’d thought dead moved his arm and pulled the dagger from his helmet. Then he staggered to his feet and raised his sword.
As if he’d only been stung by a bee.
The Slaughter Saint blinked in silence. Jeok Cheongang shook his head again, remembering the first time he’d seen one of those loathsome monsters.
“Didn’t that brat Taekyung tell you? There are damned things that openly defy the natural order set by Heaven.”
Only then did the Slaughter Saint realize who stood before them. He let out a low groan.
“...Black Ghosts.”

He’d already heard what had happened in Gansu. There were monsters that got back up no matter how many times they were killed, and every one of them had once been a fiend who dominated the Demonic Cult.
“I heard they were like the legendary living jiangshi. So it was true.”
“Worse bastards than living jiangshi. You can tell just by watching them move, can’t you?”
Jeok Cheongang stood beside the Slaughter Saint and gathered his internal energy once more. The Black Ghosts, now six in number, were closing in from all sides.
“How do we take them down?”
“I’ve heard there are only two ways. First, keep killing them until they die.”
Fwoosh.
White flames rolled over Jeok Cheongang’s hands. They lit the strangely dark space, revealing the Black Ghosts approaching with their eerie noises and the enemy forces packed tightly around them.
They also revealed other figures, hidden deep within that vast encirclement, controlling them.
“Second, cut off their heads and disable their arms and legs.”
And at that moment—
BOOM!
Jeok Cheongang thrust out both palms with all his might. Waves of flame scattered in every direction as he kicked off the ground and shot forward.
“Defend!”
—GRAAAAAH!
The shouts of humans and monsters mingled.
A path of fire opened through the enemies surrounding them. The Black Ghosts held their ground before Jeok Cheongang, but a sharp gust swept past their angled legs.
Whoosh. Slice!
The sword swinging toward Jeok Cheongang flew into the air. The Slaughter Saint had severed the arm of the first Black Ghost to charge.
“Go!”
The shout was brief, but its meaning was clear. Jeok Cheongang gave a small nod and advanced without slowing, clenching his fist.
Rrrrrk.
At the heart of the shimmering heat, white flame gathered around the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, brought to the utmost limit of its power.
Even the monster standing nearly thirty feet tall and the Dark Heaven faithful packed into a defensive line widened their eyes at the heat.
And in that instant, when time itself seemed to stop—
“I am the—”
Jeok Cheongang’s fist shot forward, crushing the wind.
“Fire King!”
KWA-A-A-A-A!
Space warped. The ground sank.
Horrific heat melted the flesh and bones of everything in its path. A flash of white so brilliant it hardly seemed possible for flame blotted out his view.
Fwoosh—KRRRUMBLE!
The light faded as quickly as it had come. Jeok Cheongang saw what lay before him and finally released the breath he’d been holding.
Huu.
Heat poured between his trembling lips like flame from a weary fire dragon.
He had poured out all his strength, but the joy of accomplishing what he’d set out to do was greater than the exhaustion.
Sizzle. Szzzz.
The green ground was gone. All that remained was a hellscape spread between the scorched earth, black as a volcanic region, and a pale haze of steam.
Fsssh.
A hot wind blew from somewhere, and the bodies that had barely held their shape crumbled.
Monsters and humans alike. Even one unlucky Black Ghost who had stood directly in Jeok Cheongang’s path.
With a single strike, hundreds of enemies had turned to ash and scattered. The same had happened beyond the thick veil of steam, which now spread dozens of yards in every direction.
At least, that was what Jeok Cheongang thought.
Then his senses caught something wrong.
Ssshhh.
An unseen current of qi crept through the ground and air. The moment he felt it, Jeok Cheongang realized what was amiss.
...This is.
Perhaps pouring out all his strength had left him too exhausted to notice at first.
Looking back, it had been strange from the start. How had such a dense, vast cloud of steam formed?
And why had the enemies beyond it shown no reaction at all?
Cold qi.
As the two words pierced his mind, Jeok Cheongang stamped down on the ground, which was slowly freezing over. He had already forgotten the horrifying heat from moments ago.
Crack.
A chill ran through his toes. At the same time, someone’s face came to mind.
Jeok Cheongang looked at the steam with a sunken gaze and parted his lips.
“Anyone with the slightest bit of manners would greet an elder properly. You’ve got less respect than an eyelash, you little brat.”
At that moment—
KRRRACK!
The steam blocking his way split apart.
No—it shattered in midair.
Beyond the bone-chilling cold stood an immense wall of ice. And with it, the person Jeok Cheongang had just thought of.
“You noticed. That’s just like you.”
At the Grand Sorceress’s reply, Jeok Cheongang spat out a wad of phlegm.
“Yeah. I knew it was you.”
That had been a strike delivered with all his strength—more than enough to turn even the sorcerers hidden among the countless enemies to ash in an instant.
Even a Supreme Peak master on his level would have found it nearly impossible to block the damage completely.
Unless they had the strange dark arts Jin Taekyung called Magic.
“So the brat was right. You managed to stay alive.”
“An old man who should’ve died and returned to the earth long ago is still walking around. Why should this be such a surprise?”
The Grand Sorceress continued with a sneer.
“At your age, you should be resting in a back room, watching your grandchildren play. Why come all this way to play with fire?”
“If my one and only Disciple is putting on a show for me, I can play with fire a hundred times over. A thousand, even.”
“Don’t push yourself too hard. Think of your age.”
“Don’t worry. Old as I am, I can still kill you.”
For an instant, the Grand Sorceress’s eyes darkened behind her veil. She heard the certainty in his words.
Sizzle.
The ice wall was still melting, little by little, unable to withstand the heat of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist. It bore out his claim.
...Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King. So his reputation isn’t empty.

Just as the Grand Sorceress thought this to herself and cautiously gathered her energy, Jeok Cheongang, who had been watching her and the three Black Ghosts guarding her with a sunken gaze, suddenly spoke.
“But today isn’t our only chance.”
In truth, he was just as pressed for time.
The Slaughter Saint was fighting desperately, surrounded by the six—no, now five—Black Ghosts. And his Disciple, who must not die, was fighting the Blood Lord.
Their agreed time was up. Though Jeok Cheongang had hoped for more, they had accomplished enough.
“Clear the way. Before I burn you all to ashes.”
Across the distance of dozens of yards, Jeok Cheongang’s reddish-hot gaze met the Grand Sorceress’s ice-cold one.
After a brief but long silence, the Grand Sorceress’s quiet voice rang out.
“For that person’s sake, I’ll kill you. Even if it isn’t today.”
“Got any more bullshit to say?”
Jeok Cheongang gave a quiet laugh at the Grand Sorceress’s silence, then swiftly turned around.

chapters.title: Chapter 1094
paragraphs: Time was always absolute.
But the way its passage felt was relative.
For Jin Taekyung, barely half a quarter-hour had passed in a desperate exchange that seemed as though it might go on forever.
Slice!
Scorching pain flared along his side. Taekyung wondered whether his body was growing sluggish as the wounds piled up, or whether the Blood Lord was getting faster.
Or both.
But his thoughts were nothing compared to what the Blood Lord was feeling.
What... is this guy?
The Blood Lord’s eyes had blazed with rage, scattering streaks of crimson light. Now his gaze had sunk deep, and his eyes trembled faintly.
Three times.
Today marked his third encounter with Jin Taekyung.
The first time, he’d only watched from afar.
On the day the Jin Family of Taiyuan rose to become the preeminent clan of Shanxi Province, the young upstart who’d gone from the family’s disgrace to a Hidden Dragon had struck him as interesting.
At their second meeting, a year later, he’d felt more than interest.
To be honest, he’d been surprised.
Chosen as the Fire King’s Disciple, Jin Taekyung had grown almost unrecognizably strong. He’d become a young beast with even more ferocity in him.
So the Blood Lord had crushed him.
Thoroughly.

The Sword Saint’s intervention had forced the Blood Lord to retreat in humiliation, but Taekyung himself had been easy to handle. The Fire King’s teachings might have helped the young beast grow, yet the gulf between them remained as vast as heaven and earth.
Now another year had passed, and the Blood Lord faced an emotion beyond interest or surprise.
Astonishment.
...Why? Why won’t you fall?
He knew what had happened, of course. Four Demon Lords and Demon Empresses had met their ends at the hands of a man who’d once been nothing more than a young upstart.
But he couldn’t make himself understand it.
How had that happened? How could Taekyung stand against him without giving ground, when the Blood Lord’s own might had advanced even further?
“You!”
Crimson light surged in his eyes once more. A larger, more powerful arc of blade Force shot toward Jin Taekyung.
Whoosh—slice!
Severed strands of hair fluttered through the air. Wind pressure tore the skin exposed by Taekyung’s already-ragged clothes.
But that was all.
He slipped past the blade Force by barely a handspan and lunged forward without slowing.
Whoosh.
The distance between them vanished.
At the same time, a flash of light shot from far away, streaking over Taekyung’s shoulder as he charged.
Another Force arrow. The Blood Lord was sick of them by now.
The Bow Saint...!
He gritted his teeth and brought the Red Blade down.
KWA-ANG!
Force clashed with Force.
Through the split-second opening, a palm strike wreathed in searing heat shot toward him.
Fwoosh!
The space around them wavered. Rising wisps of heat shimmered through his vision like a dream.
The Blood Lord didn’t hesitate.
“How dare you!”
His shout rang out, charged with internal energy. He thrust out his free hand and seized the flames just before they reached him.
No—the palm behind them. Taekyung’s palm.
KRRK!
Hand met hand. Crimson Force and flame collided and twisted together.
A terrible burning pain came with them, enough to make an ordinary person faint on the spot.
Sizzle.
The Bow Saint’s intervention had delayed the Blood Lord’s counterattack by half a beat. But even as his flesh burned, he didn’t blink.
Instead, he growled at Taekyung, whose attack he had stopped. His voice was low, as though he were making a vow to himself.
“Did you think this would be enough to break me?”
He knew pain well.
He’d been in situations that should have killed him not just a few times, but dozens of times over. He had always risen again.
Through the blessing his master had bestowed on him. Through his own will.
“How dare a wretch like you—!”
Taekyung spoke quietly.
“You mean wretches. Plural.”
“What?”
The question escaped the Blood Lord before he knew it.
Whoooosh!
The sound of powerful movements swept in from every direction.
As the thick dust cloud slowly dispersed, the indistinct figures within it came into view.
“Sorry I’m late, Benefactor.”
Cheongpung’s voice was unusually subdued. His eyes had turned deep purple, and qi from the Zaha Divine Technique enveloped his body.
Over his shoulder, two aged but clear voices rang out.
“Infinite Life Buddha. At last, I meet the unwelcome guest who came to our mountain.”
“So you’re that vicious fiend.”
Cheongheoja and Perfected Being Hyeoncheon.
Cheongpung had appeared, followed by the Sect Leaders of Kunlun and Kongtong. The Blood Lord’s brow twitched.
But he had also spotted someone who troubled him more.
The Bow Saint.
She stood silently with her great bow aimed at him, steady as stone. The Blood Lord couldn’t afford to underestimate her, least of all now.
And they weren’t the last to arrive.
“I had a dream once. Shakyamuni, or whatever the hell his name was, came to me and said something.”
Step.
Footsteps reached the Blood Lord’s ears a moment late. The master who had returned to his one and only Disciple continued, his voice seething.
“Hong Dao. He told me to burn the bastard who killed that damned monk until there wasn’t a hair left of him.”
“I figured it had to be nonsense, coming from you. But I’ll believe you this once. I had a similar idea myself, though not quite the same.”
“It’s true.”
“Fine, let’s say it is. Though I doubt Shakyamuni called anyone a bastard.”

The Slaughter Saint had appeared like a ghost, without the slightest warning, and joined the encirclement. The Blood Lord suddenly felt as though he stood amid a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords.
Including Jin Taekyung, he faced no fewer than seven Supreme Peak masters. Two of them were among the Three Saints; another stood foremost among the Ten Kings and was fully their equal.
It was no mere illusion.
“So this is what you were after?”
Crack.
A bone shifted between their locked hands.
The Blood Lord’s hand had charred so badly it seemed ready to melt, yet it forced back the flames through sheer, unbelievable recovery.
Sizzle. Slither.
He tightened his grip as the flesh burned and healed, burned and healed. A growling laugh escaped him.
“But look. Which of us is really surrounded?”
Jin Taekyung didn’t answer.
More precisely, he couldn’t. The Blood Lord’s internal energy poured endlessly through their joined hands, backed by strength no human should possess. Holding against it took everything Taekyung had.
Yet his steady gaze and sharpened senses still registered everything around him.
Another vast encirclement stretched across a radius of hundreds of zhang.
And at its front and center stood—
Black Ghosts.
Them.
Beings reborn from the pit of death. Death Knights cursed with something close to immortality.
In another world, they were called Death Knights. Taekyung could sense them clearly. More than ten stood like an iron wall, giving off suffocating demonic qi.
He could sense someone behind them, too.
The Grand Mage. No—the Grand Sorceress.
He’d expected as much. She wasn’t someone who would die that easily.
But expecting it did nothing to lessen the weight of the reality before him.
At this rate, we’ll all die together.
Perhaps the outcome would be even worse.

The Blood Lord and the Grand Sorceress had gained greater martial might and supernatural abilities since the Shaolin Bloodshed. Even if Taekyung and the others brought down every Black Ghost, there was no telling what those two might do.
He wasn’t the only one torn at this crossroads.
Must I truly let this man live?
The Blood Lord asked the question in his heart, wishing he could put it to his master.
He knew how badly the Lord of Heaven wanted the accursed man before him. No one in the world deserved that title more than his master.
That was why, when he’d heard that four Demon Lords and Demon Empresses had died one after another, he’d mocked and cursed them instead.
Was it simply because they’d been weak?
Only in part.
He’d cursed them because, contrary to their master’s orders, they had brought Jin Taekyung to the brink of death again and again.
But...
Now I understand why those bastards tried to kill you.
At last, he understood how they’d felt.
And yet he understood his master even less. Why did the Lord of Heaven want Jin Taekyung so badly—a man who thwarted Dark Heaven at every turn and was growing at a rate without precedent in history?
Why did he care more about Taekyung’s safety than about the loyal servants who had always been ready to give their lives for him?
Lord of Heaven. My one and only master. Please tell this servant.
Tell him to cut down this bright-yellow sprout now.
No—Taekyung had already grown into a towering tree. Tell him to kill the man by any means necessary.
The Blood Lord pleaded more desperately than ever.
But that was all.
His voice would not reach his master. Nothing would change.
Grit.
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth and wrenched his hand away, putting all the fury surging through him into the motion.
KWA-ANG!
The boom drove Taekyung back ten steps. The Blood Lord spat out each word.
“There won’t be a next time. I’ll kill you. No matter what.”
At that moment—
Bwoooooo!
A deep, resonant horn sounded in the distance, cutting straight through the taut tension.

A terrible burning pain came with them, enough to make an ordinary person faint on the spot.
Sizzle.
The Bow Saint’s intervention had delayed the Blood Lord’s counterattack by half a beat.
But even as his flesh burned, he didn’t blink.
Instead, he growled at Taekyung, whose attack he had stopped.
His voice was low, as though he were making a vow to himself.
“Did you think this would be enough to break me?”
He knew pain well.
He’d been in situations that should have killed him not just a few times, but dozens of times over.
He had always risen again.
Through the blessing his master had bestowed on him.
Through his own will.
“How dare a wretch like you—!”
Taekyung spoke quietly.
“You mean wretches.
Plural.”
“What?”
The question escaped the Blood Lord before he knew it.
Whoooosh!
The sound of powerful movements swept in from every direction.
As the thick dust cloud slowly dispersed, the indistinct figures within it came into view.
“Sorry I’m late, Benefactor.”
Cheongpung’s voice was unusually subdued.
His eyes had turned deep purple, and qi from the Zaha Divine Technique enveloped his body.
Over his shoulder, two aged but clear voices rang out.
“Infinite Life Buddha.
At last, I meet the unwelcome guest who came to our mountain.”
“So you’re that vicious fiend.”
Cheongheoja and Perfected Being Hyeoncheon.
Cheongpung had appeared, followed by the Sect Leaders of Kunlun and Kongtong.
The Blood Lord’s brow twitched.
But he had also spotted someone who troubled him more.
The Bow Saint.
She stood silently with her great bow aimed at him, steady as stone.
The Blood Lord couldn’t afford to underestimate her, least of all now.
And they weren’t the last to arrive.
“I had a dream once.
Shakyamuni, or whatever the hell his name was, came to me and said something.”
Step.
Footsteps reached the Blood Lord’s ears a moment late.
The master who had returned to his one and only Disciple continued, his voice seething.
“Hong Dao.
He told me to burn the bastard who killed that damned monk until there wasn’t a hair left of him.”
“I figured it had to be nonsense, coming from you.
But I’ll believe you this once.
I had a similar idea myself, though not quite the same.”
“It’s true.”
“Fine, let’s say it is.
Though I doubt Shakyamuni called anyone a bastard.”
The Slaughter Saint had appeared like a ghost, without the slightest warning, and joined the encirclement.
The Blood Lord suddenly felt as though he stood amid a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords.
Including Jin Taekyung, he faced no fewer than seven Supreme Peak masters.
Two of them were among the Three Saints; another stood foremost among the Ten Kings and was fully their equal.
It was no mere illusion.
“So this is what you were after?”
Crack.
A bone shifted between their locked hands.
The Blood Lord’s hand had charred so badly it seemed ready to melt, yet it forced back the flames through sheer, unbelievable recovery.
Sizzle.
Slither.
He tightened his grip as the flesh burned and healed, burned and healed.
A growling laugh escaped him.
“But look.
Which of us is really surrounded?”
Jin Taekyung didn’t answer.
More precisely, he couldn’t.
The Blood Lord’s internal energy poured endlessly through their joined hands, backed by strength no human should possess.
Holding against it took everything Taekyung had.
Yet his steady gaze and sharpened senses still registered everything around him.
Another vast encirclement stretched across a radius of hundreds of zhang.
And at its front and center stood—
Black Ghosts.
Them.
Beings reborn from the pit of death.
Death Knights cursed with something close to immortality.
In another world, they were called Death Knights.
Taekyung could sense them clearly.
More than ten stood like an iron wall, giving off suffocating demonic qi.
He could sense someone behind them, too.
The Grand Mage.
No—the Grand Sorceress.
He’d expected as much.
She wasn’t someone who would die that easily.
But expecting it did nothing to lessen the weight of the reality before him.
At this rate, we’ll all die together.
Perhaps the outcome would be even worse.
The Blood Lord and the Grand Sorceress had gained greater martial might and supernatural abilities since the Shaolin Bloodshed.
Even if Taekyung and the others brought down every Black Ghost, there was no telling what those two might do.
He wasn’t the only one torn at this crossroads.
Must I truly let this man live?
The Blood Lord asked the question in his heart, wishing he could put it to his master.
He knew how badly the Lord of Heaven wanted the accursed man before him.
No one in the world deserved that title more than his master.
That was why, when he’d heard that four Demon Lords and Demon Empresses had died one after another, he’d mocked and cursed them instead.
Was it simply because they’d been weak?
Only in part.
He’d cursed them because, contrary to their master’s orders, they had brought Jin Taekyung to the brink of death again and again.
But...
Now I understand why those bastards tried to kill you.
At last, he understood how they’d felt.
And yet he understood his master even less.
Why did the Lord of Heaven want Jin Taekyung so badly—a man who thwarted Dark Heaven at every turn and was growing at a rate without precedent in history?
Why did he care more about Taekyung’s safety than about the loyal servants who had always been ready to give their lives for him?
Lord of Heaven.
My one and only master.
Please tell this servant.
Tell him to cut down this bright-yellow sprout now.
No—Taekyung had already grown into a towering tree.
Tell him to kill the man by any means necessary.
The Blood Lord pleaded more desperately than ever.
But that was all.
His voice would not reach his master.
Nothing would change.
Grit.
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth and wrenched his hand away, putting all the fury surging through him into the motion.
KWA-ANG!
The boom drove Taekyung back ten steps.
The Blood Lord spat out each word.
“There won’t be a next time.
I’ll kill you.
No matter what.”
At that moment—
Bwoooooo!
A deep, resonant horn sounded in the distance, cutting straight through the taut tension.

chapters.title: Chapter 1095
paragraphs: Bwooo! Bwooooooo!
The deep, resonant sound of a horn carried across hundreds of jang and pierced Jin Taekyung’s ears. He was suddenly sure he’d heard a similar sound before.
In a damp, pitch-dark land thousands of li away, at the very southern edge.
...No way.
A suspicion flashed through his mind. Eyes wide, he stared toward the sound.
And at last, he saw them.
Enormous creatures were charging through a thick cloud of dust in the distance. Even from this far away, their great swinging trunks were unmistakable.
Those are...
Elephants.
The largest, strongest creatures alive—not just among beasts, but among everything that lived on land or in rivers.
The people of the Central Plains called them xiang—elephants—and regarded them as mysterious animals. But to a few people, Jin Taekyung among them, they were fairly familiar.
For a brief time, they’d lived among people who shared their home with countless animals, trained and tamed them, and carved beautiful horns from elephants’ tusks after they died.
“Nanman Beast Palace! The Nanman Beast Palace is here!”
On the nearby wall, Hyuk Mujin spotted the herd—hundreds of elephants by his rough estimate—and shouted, brimming with excitement.
“See that, you bastards?!”
Barely fifteen minutes ago, he’d stood on the wall swallowing nervously as he watched the fierce battle below. Not anymore.
“Come on, then! Let’s have a proper fight! We’re not so badly outnumbered now!”
He had good reason to be confident.
Soon after the enormous upheaval caused by the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s scheme had been brought under control, the Nanman Beast Palace had begun to move in earnest.
No—“move” hardly did it justice. It was a migration on a staggering scale.
They’d purged every diseased shoot that had grown within their ranks. Then they’d gone further, abandoning the homeland where their ancestors had lived since time immemorial.

Beast Miao King Yayul Cheok had been furious at Dark Heaven’s scheme, which had drenched Nanman’s jungles in blood. He’d grieved the death of his sworn brother Baeksang more than anyone. And he’d been deeply moved by the outsiders from the Central Plains who had saved his people from that terrible crisis.
United at last under the Beast Miao King, the Nanman Beast Palace swore to join the Murim Alliance and avenge their people. Then they left their bloodstained homeland.
Every last one of Nanman’s tens of thousands of people went with them, along with the countless ferocious beasts they commanded.
And the fact that the Nanman Beast Palace’s forces—who should have been in Sichuan—had appeared here meant something else, too.
“The Nanman Beast Palace, the Sichuan Tang Clan, Qingcheng, and Emei must have come together! You’re all dead now!”
At Hyuk Mujin’s shout, his fist clenched tight, the allies on the wall finally brightened. Until then, Dark Heaven’s overwhelming forces had left them frozen stiff.
“Waaah!”
“Reinforcements! The reinforcements are here!”
“Yeah, you bastards! Let’s have a proper fight!”
The Nanman Beast Palace’s forces were said to be practically a small kingdom in their own right. And now they had three great sects with them, each representing the very heart of the martial world.
Those who had already resigned themselves to defeat and those who had been clinging to hope while forcing down their fear all cheered at the top of their lungs, as if they’d never felt either.
But amid the wave of joy sweeping the wall, one man gazed at the approaching dust cloud with eyes that had only grown darker.
The Nanman Beast Palace and the other three Sichuan factions? They couldn’t possibly have left Sichuan unguarded.
Sitting on Taishan’s unusually high shoulder, Namho slowly retraced his thoughts as he watched beyond the wall with a seasoned gaze.
The strength of the Nanman Beast Palace. The current state of Sichuan’s Murim, already dealt a tremendous blow by the chain of events centered on the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
And the reason he’d thought they couldn’t come.
Sichuan is one of the largest regions in the world. With front lines that extensive, the imperial army alone wouldn’t be enough. So how could they...?
The world today was like a steep mountainside where even the boundary between Murim and the state had disappeared.
The snowball that was Dark Heaven had been rolling for half a century. By now, the enemy was a boulder weighing ten thousand geun, tumbling down the slope and about to crush the villages below.
No—the entire world.
That was why the Murim Alliance couldn’t have found a way to rescue Qinghai under these circumstances.
Leave the slightest gap, and Dark Heaven would drive into it like a sharp awl.
Not merely piercing the surface. With the bizarre sorcery of a Moving Formation, they could reach somewhere deep inside.
And Sichuan’s Murim was in worse shape than any other region of the Central Plains.
Worse than bad. Its situation could hardly have been more dire.
Enemies appearing like ghosts somewhere within Sichuan weren’t the only threat it faced.
If they really have abandoned their base to save us, the enemies across Sichuan’s border in Tibet could march straight through it and into the Central Plains...
The countless thoughts tangled together in Namho’s mind, looping and colliding, vanished all at once.
A chill ran down his spine. As he froze, a low exclamation reached his ears.
“Would you look at all those elephants in one place. What a sight from up here. Glad I stayed.”
Great Sir.
It was him.
Unlike Bow Saint, Cheongpung, and the other Supreme Peak masters, he had stubbornly held his position until now. He muttered in a carefree tone, like a spectator enjoying the view.
“Strange, though. I heard you can barely breathe just standing still in Nanman, but do all its people shave their heads like that?”
Namho, who had gone blank with shock, whipped around to face him.
“What... What on earth are you talking about?”
“What do you mean? I’m just saying what I see.”
Great Sir tilted his head and pointed at the dust cloud slowly drawing nearer from hundreds of jang away.
From atop the wall, dozens of jang high, his Supreme Peak eyesight let him see what no one else could.
No.
Through the pale dust, so thick it seemed impossible to make out anything an inch ahead, thousands of people in red and yellow robes were advancing behind the elephants.
“Huh? Wait. Now that I look again...”
Great Sir stared hard at them, scratching his chin, then added:
“They look a bit like monks.”
At that moment—
A shout burst from the lips of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent, who was nearing eighty. Even Namho startled himself with its volume.
“You goddamn bastard! That’s the Potala Palace!”
At the same moment—
Bwooooooo!
To the deep, resonant sound of the horn, the Potala Palace’s army charged like mad, hundreds of elephants leading the way.
There was an undeniable gap between the modern world of the twenty-first century and this one.
Some things were similar. Others were a little different.
And the land people here called Xizang, tens of thousands of li from the Central Plains and counted among the Outer Lands, fell closer to the latter as far as I understood it.
Xizang.
In Murim, I alone knew its other name: Tibet.
And there was another religious group living there within its own little world—the Potala Palace.
That was the identity of the enormous dust cloud that had suddenly appeared.
Bwooooo!
Hundreds of elephants trumpeted at once as they charged like mad.
Now that I could see them better, their tusks, which ought to have been long and beautiful, were blackened as if they’d been deep-fried somewhere. Their bloodshot eyes looked completely gone.
Those things... are elephants?
As they drew closer by the second, I felt it again.
They were different. On another level entirely.
They were nothing like the elephants I’d seen behind the bars at the zoo when I was a kid holding my mom’s hand. Or the ones I’d seen in Nanman.
Their size, their madness, their ferocity. All of it.
Dumbo, the baby elephant I’d seen as a kid?
Give me a fucking break.
If the original author had used these lunatics as inspiration, the cartoon I’d watched would’ve been called He’s Just a Baby, but He’s a Fucking Strong Elephant: Heavenly Demon’s Reign.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The earth shook as if they really were using the Heavenly Demon’s Reign.
No, that wasn’t enough. Now the ground was splitting open.
Faced with real-life versions of the giant elephants from that movie about little folk destroying a ring, Cheongpung murmured, half dazed, “Whoa. I’ve never seen anything like that in my life...”
Neither have I, shit.
The words nearly escaped, but I managed to hold them back.
Why?
Simple.
Even without the Potala Palace rapidly closing the distance, Dark Heaven’s forces still surrounded us on every side, packed tightly around us even now.
“They arrived sooner than expected. How fortunate.”
The Blood Lord spoke with a relaxed smile.
“Of course, it’s the worst possible luck for you.”
I tightened my grip on the shaft of my spear instead of answering.
This was getting worse by the second.
We were already at a disadvantage, and now the Potala Palace from Tibet had joined Dark Heaven, too.
They never cared about Sichuan in the first place.
It wasn’t as if I’d never considered this possibility. I’d just thought it unlikely.
So had most people.
We believed Dark Heaven had drawn in the Potala Palace, which had been quietly staying in Tibet, to block the front lines in Sichuan and stop any reinforcements from reaching Qinghai Province.
We were wrong.
What the Blood Lord—or rather, the Lord of Heaven behind him—wanted from what was happening in Qinghai wasn’t some foothold from which to advance into the Central Plains.
Me. It was me.
With that realization, a huge rock seemed to press down on one corner of my chest.
So heavy it made me ache.
“Why?”
The question slipped out before I knew it.
The Blood Lord understood what I meant and answered readily.
“Do you think a fishing rod cast over a lake knows what its owner is thinking?”
“What?”
“I don’t know, either. I only do as my master commands. If he’d had them attack Sichuan, they might have opened a route into the Central Plains... but the Lord of Heaven had other ideas.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll keep my promise to spare you today. But understand this: you’re already caught in a net. One you’ll never escape.”
Then the Blood Lord’s low Sound Transmission pierced my ears.
I’ll give you one day. If you sever your Sinews and Meridians and surrender of your own accord within that time, I’ll spare everyone but you.
He slowly raised a hand and smiled at me as I stood frozen.
I swear by the name of the Lord of Heaven, that person who is my one and only light and sky. This is my last mercy—and the only way to save your people.
That was the end of it.
As the encirclement parted at the Blood Lord’s gesture, the scornful smile on his lips stabbed into my chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 1096
paragraphs: Rumble, rumble, rumble.
The enormous, heavy iron gates of Xining slowly opened their mouths.
The Grand Sorceress watched the backs of their enemies as they passed through the encirclement, parted at the Blood Lord’s signal, and headed for the gates. Then she spoke.
“Don’t you think you let them go too easily?”
“Perhaps. But...”
The Blood Lord replied in a low voice, then nodded toward the towering city walls.
“If we’d fought them then and there, our losses would’ve been considerable, too.”
The Grand Sorceress agreed, at least to a point.

Qinghai was a frontier among frontiers, a province that had stood prepared against foreign invasion since ancient times. Its walls, built from enormous blocks of dressed stone, were sturdier than anything in the Central Plains. Silver arrowheads already glinted along their tops.
And beyond Xining’s slowly opening gates stood a forest of spears and blades.
“Cornered, they would’ve fought all the harder. They still have teeth to bite with.”
Even a lowly rat would charge a cat if it thought its life was at stake. How much more fiercely would those people fight?
They had no fewer than seven Supreme Peak masters among them.
No—eight, counting the mysterious Great Sir who had never come down from the walls.
Then there were the Qinghai martial artists and imperial troops who had gathered in Xining early, with barely any losses. The Blood Lord’s judgment wasn’t wrong.
Of course, the Grand Sorceress thought there was another, more decisive reason for his choice.
He wasn’t certain. He wasn’t certain he could capture Jin Taekyung as that person wished—or, for that matter, that they could win outright.
But she kept the thought to herself. She could hardly stand the Blood Lord, yet they served the same master and pursued the same goal. There was no need to touch a nerve now.
At the same time, she could partly understand why he’d let Jin Taekyung and the other Supreme Peak masters leave without resistance.
“Well, it’s a shame, but there’s nothing to be done. I wasn’t the one that person first entrusted with Qinghai.”
“That’s unusual. I never expected to hear you say that.”
“I can separate business from personal feelings. I knew it would be a difficult battle, too.”
There were levels even among Supreme Peak masters, and the seven they’d just surrounded were far from ordinary.

Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon, whose exploits had been somewhat overshadowed by Jin Taekyung’s. Judging by innate martial talent alone, it wouldn’t have been strange to call him the greatest of all time.
Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and Cheongheoja, leaders of the venerable Daoist lineages of Kongtong and Kunlun.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint, who needed no introduction, and the Fire King Jeok Cheongang, their equal.
And finally, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung, who had proven through his every action that his very existence was a variable.
Looking at that overwhelming, dazzling lineup, even the Black Ghosts—nearly immortal as they were—seemed to fade into the background.
“If we’d fought, those things would have been wiped out, whether we survived or not.”
The Grand Sorceress gestured toward the silent Black Ghosts.
“Though one has already melted away without leaving so much as its shape behind.”
Jeok Cheongang’s full-strength strike had been that powerful. It had even broken through part of the defensive magic she’d cast.
“And there’d be no question of it if the Bow Saint and Slaughter Saint joined in. Besides, there’s something about Jin Taekyung that even I can’t quite understand.”
In Murim, where strength ruled above all, the logic of power was simple. The strong devoured the weak; the weak were trampled. That was how the world worked.
But from what the Grand Sorceress had seen, Jin Taekyung stood further outside that logic than anyone.
Even if he’d received help from those around him whenever he faced a life-or-death crisis, defeating four Demon Lords and a Demon Empress hadn’t been mere luck.
She could understand why he was called the Chosen One.
“That must be it. There’s something special about him, and that’s why that person is so obsessed with him.”
A faint note of wonder entered her voice. The Blood Lord’s lips twisted.
Obsessed. Is that what it is?
He watched the gates slowly closing. More precisely, he watched Jin Taekyung’s back disappear between them.
And he remembered what he’d said moments before.
Do you think a fishing rod cast over a lake knows what its owner is thinking?
He hadn’t said it only to Jin Taekyung. It was a self-mocking question directed at himself—and a plaintive complaint to the Lord of Heaven, who wasn’t there to hear it.
Why is that brat special to you? Why, exactly?
At that moment, the person the Blood Lord most wanted to kill wasn’t Mae Jonghak, who had once taken his arm, or Jeok Cheongang.
It was Jin Taekyung.

A greenhorn who had grown into a towering tree in barely two years. He was no longer a bright-yellow sprout the Blood Lord could crush underfoot. He had deep roots and thick branches now, yet his master still would not let his servants cut him down.
Lord of Heaven. What is it you truly want? This foolish servant cannot begin to guess.
A fishing rod.
Even if it broke against the strength of a great fish that had taken the bait, its owner could simply replace it.
The three words he’d spoken of his own accord, and the meaning they carried, weighed unusually heavily on the Blood Lord’s heart.
That was when it happened.
Bwooooo!
A horn sounded, long and deep. The Potala Palace’s army slowed to a halt some twenty-odd zhang away.
Of the hundreds of elephants standing like iron towers, thirteen of the largest and most lavishly adorned moved forward.
Thud. Thud.
The Blood Lord slowly raised his head as a vast shadow fell across his face. The elephants reached him, their heavy footfalls rumbling. A voice came down from atop their heads.
“It has been a long time, donor.”

Anyone from the Central Plains might have snorted at the halting Han speech. But the immense internal energy and authority behind the voice belonged to the grand master of a sect. It carried unmistakable anger, too.
“And yet...”
Thirteen figures dropped to the ground with a rush of displaced air.
At their center stood an old monk, slender and bony as a withered tree.
“If this humble monk has not mistaken what he sees, then I believe a convincing explanation is in order.”
The old monk ruled Tibet like a kingdom. He was the Palace Lord of the Potala Palace—or, as his people had called him by ancient custom, the Dalai Lama. He fixed his piercing gaze on the Blood Lord.
“Why did you let them go? I may be old, and my eyes may be failing, but even from a distance I could tell they were no ordinary people.”
Roused from his thoughts, the Blood Lord glanced at the gates, now firmly shut. Then he gave the Dalai Lama, who had brought a substantial force to join them, a warm smile.
“As expected of the Palace Lord. You saw them clearly.”
The Dalai Lama did not smile back, despite the Blood Lord’s unusually friendly manner.

What he’d just seen touched on one of the chief reasons the head of his fiercely insular sect had accepted Dark Heaven’s proposal decades ago and formed an alliance. It was also one of the main reasons he’d gathered the Potala Palace’s forces from across Tibet and brought them all the way to Qinghai.
“Then forgive this old monk for asking, just in case.”
When he continued, his voice was so cold that no trace of his halting speech remained.
“Were any of the enemies you just let go among those I’ve been searching for?”
At that moment, the Grand Sorceress’s lips moved behind her tightly woven silver-white veil.
I’m only saying this in case, but... don’t forget. Until we achieve our goal, the Potala Palace is a rather useful card to have.
Her warning reached the Blood Lord before he could answer. His lips twisted despite himself.
Our goal?
Ordinarily, he would have let the phrase pass. Now, for some reason, it struck him as absurd.
She and he were both fishing rods, after all. Someone could replace them whenever they pleased.
I’ve had only one goal from the beginning: to serve that person with body and soul, and help him rule as the master and father of all under heaven.
But why?
Why did he find himself thinking that his master, the great Lord of Heaven, wanted not the vast world, but one young man?
“Ha.”
A quiet laugh escaped him before he could stop it.
The Dalai Lama’s gaze grew darker.
“I’m still waiting for an answer.”
Amusement in his voice, the Blood Lord replied, “Surely you’ve already guessed.”
“Does that mean...?”

“That’s right. The Fire King Jeok Cheongang. And the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. The Fire Gate Clan’s scions you’ve searched for so desperately were among them. Ah, come to think of it...”
He extended a finger toward the ground at the Dalai Lama’s feet.
“I believe they were standing right where you are now. Only moments ago, of course.”
The air around them shook with the aura pouring from the Dalai Lama and the Twelve Secret Monks, the Potala Palace’s finest fighters.
“You let them go so easily? Even knowing how much I—how much we—hate the Fire Gate Clan?”
His voice was as dry as a desert of burning sand. The ruler of Tibet’s vast martial world was furious.
The Fire Gate Clan.
A cursed name every Secret Monk of the Potala Palace knew and none could forget.
They were the ones who had driven the Potala Palace’s transformation from a Buddhist sect known for its excessive belligerence into a theocratic state with formidable martial power.
“How dare you break your promise? What do you think you’re doing?”
“Well, now...”
The Dalai Lama glared at him with a frost-sharp aura, speaking down to him as though it were the most natural thing in the world. The Blood Lord gave a short laugh.
“Don’t worry. I remember perfectly well. That heartrending story from two hundred years ago, and the close bond behind our promise.”
“What?”
The Dalai Lama’s eyes widened at the offhand reply. The Blood Lord continued quietly.
“But unlike me, Palace Lord, you seem to have forgotten something.”
“Forgotten? What are you talking about?”
“You know better than anyone how much help that person gave you in making the Potala Palace what it is today.”
“That...”
The Dalai Lama bit his lip, unable to finish. The Blood Lord clicked his tongue.
“As I said, I’ll keep my promise. If you play a substantial part in capturing Jin Taekyung, I’ll put the Fire King in your custody and give you a generous reward besides.”
The Dalai Lama was silent for a moment before speaking heavily.
“How can I believe you?”
“What, you don’t trust me?”
“I trust that person. But you let them go right before my eyes, when we had the perfect opportunity.”
A sneer touched the Blood Lord’s lips. It wasn’t the Dalai Lama’s distrust that offended him. He found it laughable that the man truly believed what he’d said.

Even accounting for Dark Heaven’s full support, the strength the Potala Palace had amassed was undeniable. The Dalai Lama was its greatest master; he could stand against any one of the Ten Kings besides Jeok Cheongang without being outmatched.
But...
That’s as far as you go.
It wasn’t a question of martial skill.
It was a question of the size of one’s inner self. Of the person one was.
The Grand Sorceress had already understood what the Blood Lord intended when he let their enemies go, and had said nothing. The Dalai Lama could only lament the great fish he’d watched slip away.
“Do you still not understand?”
“What is it I’m supposed to understand...?”
“I wanted to make certain of everything. To leave them no opening to escape, however small.”
The Dalai Lama was about to say something when he suddenly realized something and opened his eyes wide.
“Could it be...?”
The Blood Lord nodded without a word.

If his guess was right, it would happen today: the Yangtze River Channel League’s hundreds of ships would finally enter the Yellow River tributary leading to Qinghai, where the Green Forest Alliance would meet them alongside the ten thousand followers who had joined them in advance.
“Another day, two at most. This battle will be over within that time.”
Thirty thousand additional troops would cut through the swift current to reach Qinghai and close even the smallest gap.
They were the final key to a certain victory.
They were also why he’d given Jin Taekyung a day to think.
His promise?
He had never intended to keep it. In fact, he hoped Jin Taekyung would not be foolish enough to sever his own Sinews and Meridians.
Because only then—only if Jin Taekyung resolved to fight to the death—would the Blood Lord have grounds to kill him.
Lord of Heaven, forgive me. Even if this is not what you wish, I act only out of loyalty.
As if confessing his sins, the Blood Lord murmured to himself, then slowly parted his lips.
He turned to the Dalai Lama, who was watching him with a face much brighter than before.
“Shut your mouth. Speak down to me again, and I’ll rip that mouth apart.”
Watching the Dalai Lama freeze in place, the Blood Lord laughed wildly.
Once was enough to be treated like someone else’s fishing rod.
